Once upon a time there was a famous steam train. Every morning it would leave the station toing and froing with toots and whistles. All the people of the town would come and watch it go by. 

One day, the famous steam train went to the station and saw lots of children smiling and laughing. The steam train wanted to make them happy, so it made a joke. 

"Toot toot!" said the steam train. The children laughed and laughed. They thought it was the funniest joke ever. 

The steam train kept telling jokes while it chugged along the tracks. Everywhere it went, children were laughing and enjoying its jokes. 

From then on, the steam train became famous for telling jokes and making people smile.

"Let's go and see," Nala said.

They followed Lila to the big rock. They did not see the hunter hiding behind a tree. He had dropped the coin on purpose. He wanted to lure the animals to his trap. He had a big net under some leaves. He waited for the animals to come closer.

Lila, Tom and Nala reached the big rock. They saw more shiny things on the ground. They were more coins. They were very happy. They started to pick up the coins with their teeth and paws.

"Look, Lila, I found a silver coin!" Tom said.

"Look, Tom, I found a gold coin!" Nala said.

"Look, Nala, I found a red coin!" Lila said.

They did not notice the hunter coming out of his hiding place. He had a big smile on his face. He grabbed the end of the net and pulled it. The net fell over the animals. They were trapped. They dropped the coins and started to scream.

"Help, help, we are trapped!" Lila said.

"Let us go, let us go, you are mean!" Tom said.

"Please, please, don't hurt us, we are sorry!" Nala said.

The hunter laughed. He said, "Ha, ha, ha, you silly animals. You fell for my trick. You like shiny things, don't you? Well, now you are mine. I will take you to my house and make you into fur coats and hats. You will be very warm and cozy."

The animals were very sad and scared. They wished they had not followed the shiny things. They wished they had stayed away from the hunter. They wished they had listened to their parents, who had told them to be careful in the forest. They learned a hard lesson. Shiny things are not always good. Sometimes, they are traps.

He felt very cold and started shivering. 

Timmy wondered why he was feeling so cold. He realized that his mom was right and he should have listened to her. He ran back inside and put on his warm coat. He felt much better and was able to play outside for a long time without feeling cold anymore. 

Timmy learned an important lesson that day. He learned that it's important to listen to his mom and wear warm clothes when it's cold outside. He was happy that he didn't get sick and was able to continue having fun outside. From that day on, Timmy always wore his warm coat when he went outside in the cold. The end.

Lily was sad to hear this news. She didn't want to give away any of her books. She said to her mom, "But I love all my books! Can't we keep them all?"

Her mom replied, "I know you love your books, but we can't take them all with us. We need to make room for new things in our new home."

Lily thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, but can we at least keep my favorite ones?" Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, we will make sure to keep your most precious books."

In the end, Lily was happy that she could keep some of her books and she learned that even though she couldn't keep everything, she was still very wealthy with the love of her family and her favorite books.

Kitty was scared, but she didn't want to fight. She said, "No, this is my hat." Spot got mad and tried to take the hat. Kitty ran away very fast. She went home and told her mom about the fight.

Kitty's mom said, "You did the right thing. It's not nice to fight." Kitty felt better and knew that she could stand up for herself without fighting. She kept wearing her big red hat and was not shy anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat cake. One day, her mommy made a big, yummy cake for her. Lily was very happy.

But Lily was a stubborn girl. She did not want to share her cake with her brother, Timmy. Timmy asked, "Lily, can I have some cake too?" Lily said, "No, this is my cake!" Timmy was sad.

Mommy saw this and said, "Lily, you need to share the cake with Timmy. If you yield some cake to him, I will make you another cake tomorrow." Lily thought about it and decided to share the cake with Timmy. They both enjoyed the cake together, and mommy was proud of Lily for not being stubborn anymore.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to the park to play. She saw a bald man sitting on a bench near the playground. The man had a big bag next to him. Amy was curious about what was in the bag.

Amy went to the man and asked, "What's in the bag?" The man smiled and said, "I have a ball to play pass with. Would you like to play with me?" Amy was excited and said, "Yes, I love to play pass!"

They started to play pass with the ball. The man threw the ball to Amy, and she caught it. Then, Amy threw the ball back to the man. They played for a long time and had lots of fun. At the end of the day, the man gave Amy the ball as a gift. Amy was very happy and thanked the man. From that day on, Amy and the bald man became good friends and played pass together every time they met at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his uncle Jack. Uncle Jack was very competitive, but Tim did not care. They both liked to play games and have fun together. One day, Tim and Uncle Jack decided to play a game of who can stretch their arms the widest.

"Let's see who can stretch more!" said Uncle Jack. Tim and Uncle Jack started to stretch their arms as wide as they could. They both tried very hard, but Uncle Jack stretched more than Tim.

"I win!" said Uncle Jack, happy that he won. Tim was sad that he lost, but he did not give up. He wanted to try again the next day.

The next day, Tim and Uncle Jack played the stretching game again. This time, Tim stretched and stretched, and he won! Uncle Jack was surprised, but he was happy for Tim. They both learned that it is okay to lose sometimes, and that trying again can help you get better. The moral of the story is to never give up and always try your best.

She was very kind and gave him a towel. She dried his feet and told him he must be careful next time. He thanked her and went back home, happy to have found a safe place in the storm. From that day on, he always listened to his mom and was careful during storms.

"Ben, are you OK?" Lily asked. She saw that Ben was sweating and frowning. "You look sad. Do you want me to help you?"

Moral value: The story teaches that pride can make us do foolish things, and that we should ask for help when we need it. It also teaches that kindness and forgiveness can heal wounds and make things better.

One day, a big bird came to the swamp. He had a camera and a hat. He said he was looking for the most beautiful frog in the swamp. He wanted to take a picture and put it in a book. All the frogs were excited and wanted to be in the book. They jumped and croaked and showed off their colors.

Bella also wanted to be in the book, but she was dirty and muddy. She had not washed for a long time. She tried to hide behind a leaf, but the bird saw her. He flew over and said, "Hello, little frog. What is your name?"

The bird smiled and said, "Don't be sad, Bella. You are not ugly. You are just different. You have a special pattern on your skin that no other frog has. It is very rare and interesting. I think you are the most beautiful frog in the swamp. Can I take your picture and put it in my book?"

Bella was surprised and happy. She said, "Really? You think I am beautiful? You want to put me in your book?"

The bird nodded and said, "Yes, I do. But first, you have to wash. Washing is good for you. It makes you clean and healthy and shiny. It also shows your true colors and your special pattern. Will you wash for me, Bella?"

Bella thought for a moment. She wanted to be in the book and be famous. She also wanted to make the bird happy. She said, "Okay, I will wash for you. But can you help me?"

The bird agreed and helped Bella wash. He splashed water on her and rubbed her gently with his feathers. He sang a song and made her laugh. Soon, Bella was clean and shiny. Bella smiled and posed for the camera. The bird took her picture and put it in his book. He said, "Thank you, Bella. You are a star. You will be famous and everyone will love you. But remember, washing is important. It makes you look good and feel good. Will you wash every day, Bella?"

Bella nodded and said, "Yes, I will. Thank you, bird. You are a good friend. You taught me a lesson. Washing is not boring. It is fun and good. I will wash every day and be happy."

The bird hugged Bella and said, "You are welcome, Bella. I am glad you learned your lesson. You are a smart and beautiful frog. I hope to see you again. Goodbye, Bella."

The bird flew away and Bella waved goodbye. She looked at the book and saw her picture. She was the first frog in the book. She was famous and happy. She hopped and played with her friends, but she also washed every day. She was the most beautiful frog in the swamp.

It is a way to remember and share our history, our values, and our love. It is a way to have fun and be happy with our family and friends. It is a way to be proud of who we are and where we come from. Do you want to join me and enjoy the festival?"

Lila looked at her mom and nodded. She realized that her mom was right. She decided to give the festival a chance. She played the games, listened to the songs, and ate the food. It was still a fairy tale, in its own way.

"Hello, little sailors," the whale said. "What are you doing in my ocean?"

Ben and Lily did not understand the whale's language. They looked at each other and frowned. They did not know what to say.

"Can you speak whale?" Ben asked Lily.

"No, can you?" Lily asked Ben.

They shook their heads. They wished they could talk to the whale and be his friend.

The whale saw their frowns and felt sad. He wanted to make them happy. He thought of an idea. He sprayed some water from his blowhole and made a rainbow in the sky.

Ben and Lily saw the rainbow and smiled. They clapped their hands and cheered. They did not need words to say thank you. They waved to the whale and he waved back.

The whale was happy too. He swam away, but not before giving them a wink. He hoped to see them again.

Ben and Lily continued their adventure. They sailed to the island and had a picnic. They shared their food with some monkeys and birds. They had a lot of fun.

They learned that even if they did not speak the same language, they could still be friends with anyone. They just needed to be kind and smile.

Bella was a pig who lived on a farm. She liked to move around and play with her friends, the other pigs. They would run, roll, dig, and splash in the mud. Bella was happy most of the time, but sometimes she felt gloomy. She wanted to see more of the world than the farm.

One day, she saw a big truck come to the farm. The farmer put some of the pigs in the truck. Bella was curious. She asked her friend Max, "Where are they going?"

Max said, "I don't know. Maybe to another farm. Maybe to a market. Maybe to a place with more mud."

Bella said, "I want to go too. I want to see new things. I want to have fun."

Max said, "But you have fun here. You have friends here. You have food here. Why do you want to leave?"

Bella said, "I don't know. I just do. Maybe I will come back. Maybe I will find something better."

She decided to sneak into the truck when the farmer was not looking. She hid under some hay and waited. The truck started to move. Bella felt excited and scared. She wondered what she would find. She hoped she would not regret her choice. She hoped she would not be gloomy.

Lily was a gifted girl. She could sing, draw and dance very well. She liked to show her skills to her friends and family. One day, she wanted to make a cup of tea for her mom, who was working at home.

She went to the kitchen and found a cup, a teabag and some water. She put the teabag in the cup and poured some water from the kettle. But the water was too hot and the cup was too heavy. She burned her hand and dropped the cup. It broke on the floor and made a big mess.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cried. She ran to her mom and showed her the red mark on her hand. Her mom hugged her and said, "Oh, sweetie, are you okay? What happened?"

"I wanted to make tea for you, but I couldn't manage the cup. It was too hot and too heavy. I'm sorry, mom. I broke the cup and made a mess," Lily said, sobbing.

Her mom kissed her hand and said, "It's okay, honey. I appreciate your thought, but you don't have to make tea for me. You're still too little to handle hot things and heavy things. Next time, ask me for help, okay? And don't worry about the cup. It was just a cup. You are more important to me than any cup."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. You are the best mom ever."

"I love you too, Lily. You are the best daughter ever. And you are very gifted. You can sing, draw and dance very well. Why don't you show me one of your skills now? Which one do you want to do?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I want to dance. Can you play some music for me?"

"Sure, let's go to the living room and dance together," her mom said.

They went to the living room and turned on the music. Lily and her mom danced and laughed and had fun. They forgot about the broken cup and the mess. They were happy.

One day, they find a big book about animals on the shelf. They want to read it together, but it is too heavy to carry. So they sit on the floor and open the book. They see lions and tigers and bears and elephants and many more. They are very excited and want to talk about the animals.

"Look, Ben, this is a lion. He is very big and strong and has a mane. He can roar very loud," Lily whispers to her brother.

"I know, Lily, he is amazing. And look, this is a tiger. He is very fast and has stripes. He can jump very high," Ben whispers back.

They whisper to each other about every animal they see, and learn many new things. They are having so much fun, they do not notice the time. They do not hear their mom calling them to go home. They do not see the librarian walking towards them.

"Excuse me, children, what are you doing here?" the librarian asks in a stern voice.

Lily and Ben look up and see her. They are scared and think they are in trouble. They close the book and stand up.

"We are sorry, miss. We were reading this book about animals. We like animals very much. We were whispering, we did not make noise," Lily says in a small voice.

The librarian looks at them and smiles. She is not angry, she is happy. She likes children who love books and animals.

"That's wonderful, children. You are very successful readers. You can whisper in the library, that's fine. But you have to listen to your mom when she calls you. She is waiting for you at the door. You can borrow this book and take it home, if you want. But you have to bring it back next week, okay?" she says in a kind voice.

Their mom is proud and happy. She hugs them and takes them home. They can't wait to read the book again. They love the library.

"Look, Ben, a lizard!" Sara says. "Can I touch it?"

Ben shakes his head. He knows lizards can run fast and bite. He is afraid of the lizard.

"No, Sara, don't touch it. It might bite you. Lizards are not nice. They eat bugs and worms. Yuck!" Ben says.

Sara and Ben run after the lizard. They hold their cookie halves in their hands. They hope the lizard will like their cookie. They hope the lizard will be their friend. They hope the lizard will let them touch it. They are happy.

"Can we climb the tree, Lily?" Tom asked.

"Let's try, Tom," Lily said. "But be careful. The tree is old. It may break."

They climbed the tree. They found a big branch. They sat on it. They looked at the park. They saw the slide, the swings, the sandbox, and the fountain. They saw other children playing. They saw birds and squirrels and butterflies.

They felt the wind. They heard the leaves. They felt the sun. They were happy.

"Look, Lily, a bell!" Tom said. "Who left it here?"

"I don't know, Tom," Lily said. "Maybe someone forgot it. Maybe it is for us."

They wanted the bell. They reached for it. They pulled the ribbon. The bell rang. It made a loud sound.

They were surprised. They heard a voice. It was from the tree.

"Hello, children," the voice said. "Thank you for finding my bell. I lost it long ago. It was a gift from a friend. I am glad you like it. You can keep it. It is yours."

They were amazed. They looked at the tree. They saw a face. It was old and kind. It had eyes and a nose and a mouth. It was smiling.

"Who are you?" Lily asked.

"I am the tree," the voice said. "I have been here for many years. I have seen many things. I have many stories. I like children. They make me happy. They play and laugh and sing. They are my friends."

They were happy. They liked the tree. They wanted to hear its stories. They wanted to be its friends.

"Can we stay with you?" Tom asked.

"Of course, you can," the voice said. "You are welcome here. You can play and learn and have fun. You can come anytime. I will always be here. I will always be your friend."

They smiled. They hugged the tree. They thanked it for the bell. They put it on the branch. They said they would come back. They climbed down the tree. They ran down the hill. They still had the purple flowers. They were happy. They had a new friend. They had a spring adventure.

"Anna, look, there is a crab in your shell!" Ben said, showing her the crab. "It is hiding in the shell!"

Anna looked at the crab. It was brown and had two claws and eight legs. It moved a little bit when Ben touched it.

"Hello, crab!" Anna said. "Why are you in the shell?"

The crab did not answer. It was shy and scared. It liked to live in the shell. The shell was its home.

"Maybe," Anna said. "But I think the crab likes the shell because it is safe and cozy and has a nice smell."

Her mom came over and looked at the bug. "That's a ladybug, Lily. They're good bugs. They eat other bugs that can hurt our plants," her mom said.

Lily was happy to learn about the ladybug. She watched it crawl off her palm and onto a nearby flower. "Thank you for telling me, Mama," Lily said with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, she was running and fell down, hurting her knee. She cried and cried until her mom came to settle her down. 

Lily's mom said, "Let's go inside and put a bandage on your knee." Lily said, "It's difficult to walk." Her mom carried her inside and put a bandage on her knee. 

The next day, Lily wanted to play outside again. Her mom said, "No, you need to rest your knee." Lily said, "But I want to play." Her mom said, "It's difficult to play when you're hurt." 

Lily was sad and didn't want to listen to her mom. She went outside to play anyway. But when she started running, she fell again and hurt her knee even more. This time, she had to go to the hospital. Her mom said, "I told you it's difficult to play when you're hurt." 

Lily learned her lesson and promised to listen to her mom from now on. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to cuddle with her soft pillow every night before sleeping. One night, Lily's pillow felt different. It was not as fluffy as before. She asked her mom, "Mommy, can you fix my pillow? It doesn't feel good anymore." 

Her mom replied, "Sure, let me fluff it up for you." After a few minutes, Lily's pillow felt better. "Thank you, Mommy! You fixed my pillow. I trust you to always make things better," said Lily. 

Her mom smiled and gave her a warm hug. "You're welcome, sweetie. I want you to have a good night's sleep. Also, I made some tasty cookies for you. Do you want to try them?" 

"Yum! I love cookies. Thank you, Mommy," said Lily, as she took a bite of the tasty cookie. She felt happy and content, knowing that her mommy always took care of her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to climb trees in her backyard. One day, she saw a big, heavy branch that she wanted to climb. 

Lily's mom came outside and saw her trying to climb the branch. "Be careful, Lily! That branch looks really heavy," said her mom. 

Lily replied, "I know, Mommy. But I want to climb it and see the band play at the park." 

Her mom smiled and said, "Okay, but be careful. We don't want you to get hurt." 

Lily climbed the branch and saw the band playing in the park. She was so happy that she climbed the heavy branch to see them.

Once upon a time, there was a pink ostrich named Rosie. Rosie lived in a big field with lots of other animals. One day, Rosie saw a little bird who had fallen out of its nest. Rosie wanted to help the bird, but the other animals laughed at her and said, "Ostriches can't fly, how can you help that bird?"

Rosie didn't give up. She used her long neck to reach the bird and put it back in its nest. The little bird's mother was so happy that she started to applaud Rosie. All the other animals saw how kind Rosie was and they felt bad for laughing at her.

The animals apologized to Rosie and they all became friends. Rosie learned that even though she was different, she could still help others and make a difference. The moral of the story is to never give up and always be kind to others, even if they are different from you.

One day, Lila and Tom are playing with dolls. Lila says, "This is my doll. She is pretty and has a dress. You can't play with her. She is mine." Tom says, "But I want to play with her. She looks fun. Can I hold her for a little bit?" Lila says, "No, you can't. You have your own toys. Go play with them."

Tom is upset. He thinks Lila is not nice. He says, "Fine. I don't want to play with you anymore. You are mean. I will go home." He picks up his ball, his teddy, and his puzzle. He walks to the door.

Lila is upset too. She thinks Tom is not fair. She says, "Fine. Go home. I don't care. I have many toys. I don't need you." She hugs her doll. She looks at her toys.

But Lila feels lonely. She misses Tom. She sees that her toys are old and dusty. She says, "Maybe I was too selfish. Maybe I should have shared my doll with Tom. He is my friend. I don't want to lose him." She puts down her doll. She runs to the door.

She sees Tom outside. He is walking slowly. He looks sad. Lila calls, "Tom, wait! I'm sorry. I was wrong. You can play with my doll. You can play with any of my toys. Please come back. I want to play with you."

Tom hears Lila. He turns around. He sees Lila smiling. He smiles too. He says, "Really? You mean it? You will share your toys with me?" Lila says, "Yes, I mean it. I will share my toys with you. You are my friend. I don't want to make you upset."

Tom and Lila hug. They are happy. They go back to Lila's room. They play with the doll, the ball, the teddy, the puzzle, and the other toys. They have fun. They are good friends.

Tom was a little bunny who liked to hop. He hopped in the garden, he hopped in the house, he hopped everywhere. One day, he saw a big armchair in the living room. It looked soft and cozy. He wanted to hop on it and rest.

He hopped up to the armchair and tried to hop on it. But it was too high for him. He hopped and hopped, but he could not reach it. He felt sad and tired. He wished he had a friend to help him.

Then he heard a voice. "Hello, little bunny. Do you need some help?" It was Lucy, the cat. She was sitting on the window sill. She saw Tom trying to hop on the armchair.

"Yes, please," said Tom. "I want to hop on the armchair, but it is too high for me. Can you help me?"

"Sure, I can help you," said Lucy. "I can jump very high. I can jump on the armchair and then lift you up. Do you want to try?"

"Yes, thank you," said Tom. He was happy to have a friend.

Lucy jumped on the armchair and then reached down with her paw. She grabbed Tom by the ears and lifted him up. She placed him next to her on the armchair. They both smiled.

"There you go, little bunny. Now you can hop on the armchair and rest," said Lucy.

"Thank you, Lucy. You are a good friend. You are a good cat," said Tom.

They snuggled together on the armchair and closed their eyes. They felt warm and comfy. They were happy.

One day, Tom sees Ben's truck and wants to play with it. He takes it from Ben and runs away. Ben is angry. He chases Tom and shouts, "Give me back my truck! It is mine!"

Tom does not listen. He drives the truck faster and faster. He does not see the chair in his way. He crashes the truck into the chair. The truck breaks. The wheel falls off and the tie that holds the trailer snaps. Tom is scared. He drops the truck and runs to his room.

Ben sees his broken truck and cries. He loves his truck. He does not know how to repair it. He goes to his mom and shows her his truck. He says, "Mom, look what Tom did! He broke my truck! Can you fix it?"

Mom hugs Ben and says, "I'm sorry, Ben. That was not nice of Tom. He should not take your truck without asking. I will try to repair it for you. Do you have some glue and tape?"

Ben nods and says, "Yes, I do. They are in my drawer. Thank you, mom."

Mom and Ben go to Ben's room. They find the glue and tape. They put the wheel back on the truck and tie the trailer with a new tie. They make the truck look like new. Ben is happy. He says, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I love you."

Ben thinks for a moment. He says, "Okay, mom. I will try. But he has to say sorry first."

Mom smiles and says, "That's a good idea, Ben. I'm sure he will."

"What do you want to buy?" Tom asked Mia.

"I want to buy a candy," Mia said. "A red candy that is sweet and spicy."

They could not agree on what to buy. They started to discuss. They talked and talked, but they did not listen to each other. They only wanted what they wanted.

Lily and Max were playing with blocks in the living room. They wanted to build a big tower, but they did not know how many blocks they needed. Lily had an idea.

"Let's measure the blocks with this tape," she said, holding a yellow tape that her dad used for his work. "Then we can count how many we have and how many we need."

Max nodded and helped Lily measure the blocks. They lined them up on the floor and put the tape next to them. They counted one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten blocks.

"That's a lot of blocks," Max said. "But I think we need more to make a big tower."

Just then, their cat, Fluffy, came into the living room. Fluffy was a nosy cat. He liked to sniff and touch everything. He saw the blocks and the tape and thought they were toys. He jumped on the blocks and knocked them over. He grabbed the tape with his paw and ran away.

"Hey, stop!" Lily shouted. "That's our tape! We need it to measure!"

Lily and Max chased Fluffy around the house, but he was too fast and sneaky. He hid under the bed, behind the couch, and on top of the fridge. He did not want to give back the tape.

Lily and Max were tired and sad. They could not build their tower without the tape. They went back to the living room and saw their blocks scattered on the floor.

"What do we do now?" Max asked.

Lily shrugged. She did not know. She wished Fluffy was not so nosy and mean.

"Maybe we can use something else to measure," she said. "Like a book, or a spoon, or a sock."

Max thought for a moment. He smiled.

"Or maybe we can just guess," he said. "And see how high we can make our tower."

Lily smiled too. She liked that idea. She picked up a block and put it on another block.

"Let's try," she said.

They started to build their tower again, without the tape. They did not care how many blocks they had or how many they needed. They just wanted to have fun. And they did.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big tree with many vines that hung down from the branches. They liked to swing on the vines and pretend they were monkeys.

One day, they saw a new vine that was very long and thick. It looked like a snake. Ben wanted to touch it, but Lily was scared.

"Don't touch it, Ben!" Lily said. "It might bite you!"

Ben laughed. "It's not a snake, Lily. It's just a vine. Look, I'll show you." He reached out his hand to grab the vine.

But as soon as he touched it, the vine moved. It wrapped around Ben's arm and pulled him up. Ben screamed. Lily screamed too.

"Help! Help!" Ben shouted. "Let me go!"

The vine did not let go. It lifted Ben higher and higher, until he was close to the top of the tree. There, he saw a big nest with many eggs. And on the nest, there was a huge bird with sharp claws and a long beak. It was a hawk. And the vine was its tail.

The hawk looked at Ben with angry eyes. It opened its beak and made a loud noise. It was hungry. And Ben looked like a tasty snack.

Lily was very scared for her brother. She did not know what to do. She looked around and saw a wise old owl sitting on a branch. The owl had seen everything.

"Please, Mr. Owl, help my brother!" Lily cried. "The hawk has him!"

The owl nodded. He knew the hawk was mean and greedy. He flew over to the hawk and said in a loud voice:

"Hey, hawk, leave the boy alone! He is not your food. He is a human. Humans are friends, not food. If you eat him, you will make his family very sad. And you will make me very angry. And you don't want to make me angry. I am bigger and stronger than you. And I have many friends who will help me. So let him go. Now!"

The hawk was surprised. He did not expect the owl to talk to him. He did not like the owl's words. He did not want to make the owl angry. He did not want to fight with the owl and his friends. He decided to let go of the vine and Ben.

Ben fell down, but the owl caught him in his wings. He brought him back to the ground, where Lily was waiting. She hugged her brother and thanked the owl.

"Thank you, Mr. Owl, you are very kind and wise!" Lily said.

"You're welcome, little girl," the owl said. "But be careful next time. Not all vines are safe. Some are part of animals. And some animals are not friendly. Always look before you touch. And always listen to your sister. She is smart and brave."

Ben nodded. He was sorry he did not listen to Lily. He learned his lesson. He thanked the owl too. And he promised to be more careful.

The owl smiled. He flew away, back to his branch. Ben and Lily went back to their house, holding hands. They were happy to be safe. And they were happy to have each other.

Amy nods and takes the package. She opens it and finds a beautiful doll. The doll has long brown hair and a pink dress. She also has a card that says, "Happy birthday, Amy. I hope you are healthy and happy. I miss you a lot. Love, Grandma."

Amy hugs the doll and says, "Wow, this is the best gift ever. I love you, Grandma. And I love you, Tom. You made my day."

Amy waves and says, "Bye, Tom. Thank you for your time. See you soon."

Tom gets in his truck and drives away. He feels happy. He likes to deliver joy to people. He is a good mailman.

Then they see a big rock near the pond. They have an idea. They take the rock and put it in the bucket. They cover it with some bread. They pretend to feed the grumpy duck.

"Here, grumpy duck, have some bread!" Ben says. "You can have it all!"

The grumpy duck is greedy and foolish. He thinks he has won. He grabs the bucket and tries to eat the bread. But he finds the rock instead. He bites the rock and hurts his beak. He drops the bucket and quacks in pain.

"Ouch, ouch, ouch!" he says. "What is this? This is not bread. This is a rock. A hard and nasty rock. You tricked me!"

Lila and Ben laugh and clap. They have taught the grumpy duck a lesson. They take the bucket and feed the other ducks. The other ducks are happy and grateful. They say thank you and share the bread. Lila and Ben smile and hug. They have fun feeding the ducks.

Suddenly, Lily remembered her mom telling her to wear socks. She wished she had listened to her mom. She ran back inside to put on her socks and felt much better. From then on, Lily always listened to her mom and put on her socks before going outside to play.

She cried for help, but no one heard her. She was alone and scared. She saw a big cat coming. The cat had sharp teeth and claws. It wanted to eat Lily.

"Mia, help me!" Ben said. He reached out his hand.

Mia saw Ben. She felt sorry for him. She ran to him and grabbed his hand. She tried to pull him up. But she was too small. She could not move him.

She looked around. She saw a big stick on the ground. She had an idea. She let go of Ben's hand and picked up the stick. She went back to the puddle.

"Ben, don't cry. I have a stick. I will poke you with the stick. Then you can push yourself up." Mia said.

She poked Ben with the stick. Ben felt the stick on his back. He pushed himself up. He got out of the puddle. He was still wet and muddy, but he was happy.

"Thank you, Mia. You are a good friend. You helped me." Ben said.

He hugged Mia. Mia hugged him back. They smiled at each other.

Lily hugged the dog and Ben. She said, "You're welcome, Ben. I'm glad you're okay. The dog is our friend. He saved you. He shared our picnic. He is brave and good."

Ben nodded. He said, "You're right, Lily. I'm sorry I was mean to you and the dog. You are kind and smart. You shared our picnic. You were safe and careful. You are my friend."

Lily smiled. She said, "You're my friend, too, Ben. Let's go home and get dry. And let's take the dog with us. Maybe we can keep him. He needs a home and a name."

They walked home with the dog. They were happy and grateful. They learned a lesson. They learned to share, to care, and to be fair.

"Put these on and rub this on your skin. The mosquitoes don't like the clothes or the smell. They will stay away from you," she said.

Tom and Lily did as she said. They put on the clothes and the lotion. They felt warm and cozy and lemony.

Tim had a big metal car that he liked to play with. It was shiny and red and had four wheels. He liked to make it go fast on the floor and make loud noises.

One day, he saw a metal coin on the table. It was shiny and round and had a face on it. He wondered if it was like his car. He picked it up and tried to make it go on the floor, but it did not move. He tried to make loud noises, but it did not sound like his car.

He was sad and confused. He wanted to know why the metal coin was not like his metal car. He went to his mom and showed her the coin. He asked her, "Mom, why is this metal not like my metal?"

His mom smiled and hugged him. She said, "Tim, this metal is not like your metal because it is a different kind of metal. It is a coin. You can use it to buy things, like candy or toys. But you cannot play with it like your car. It is not for fun, it is for money."

Tim did not understand what money was. He asked, "Mom, what is money?"

His mom said, "Money is something that people use to trade for things they want or need. For example, if I want to buy you a new car, I have to give the store some money. The store gives me the car, and I give them the money. That is how money works."

Tim thought for a moment. He said, "Mom, can I trade this coin for a new car?"

His mom laughed and said, "No, Tim, this coin is not enough money for a new car. You need a lot of coins, or bigger coins, or paper money, to buy a new car. This coin is only enough for a small thing, like a candy or a sticker."

Tim said, "Oh, I see. Then can I trade this coin for a candy?"

His mom said, "Sure, Tim, you can trade this coin for a candy. But first, you have to rub it on your shirt. That will make it clean and shiny. Then you can go to the store and buy a candy. But remember, once you trade it, you cannot get it back. You have to choose wisely."

Tim nodded and said, "OK, Mom, I will rub it on my shirt and choose wisely. Thank you for teaching me about money. You are very wise, Mom."

His mom kissed him and said, "You are very welcome, Tim. You are very smart, Tim. I love you, Tim."

Tim rubbed the coin on his shirt and made it clean and shiny. He put it in his pocket and ran to the store. He looked at all the candies and stickers and toys. He thought hard and chose wisely. He traded his coin for a candy that he liked. He ate it and smiled. He was happy and proud. He learned something new today. He loved his mom and his metal car. He was a good boy.

Lily loved the smell so much that she wanted to make her own perfume. She got some flowers from the garden and mashed them up in a bowl. Then, she added some water and stirred it all together. She had made her own perfume!

Lily was so proud of her design and her perfume. She showed her dad the castle she drew and let him smell her perfume. He told her that she was very creative and talented. Lily felt very happy and couldn't wait to design more things and make more perfume. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big spider who lived in a big house. The spider loved to spin cobwebs all around the house. One day, a little girl came to visit the house. She saw the large cobwebs and was scared. 

The spider saw the little girl and wanted to be friends with her. So, the spider crawled down from the ceiling and said hello. The little girl was still scared, but the spider told her not to worry. 

To test if the little girl was brave, the spider asked her to touch the cobweb. The little girl was scared, but she touched the cobweb anyway. The spider was happy and they became friends. From that day on, the little girl would visit the spider every day and they would play together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to follow her mommy wherever she went. One day, they went outside to hail a taxi. Lily saw a big, yellow taxi and she pointed at it. "Mommy, can we ride in that taxi?" she asked. 

Mommy nodded and they got inside the taxi. The taxi driver was a humble man with a big smile. "Where to?" he asked. 

Lily's mommy told the driver their destination, but the driver took a wrong turn. Lily noticed that they were going the wrong way. "Mommy, the taxi is going the wrong way!" she said. 

Mommy told the driver to turn around, and they eventually arrived at their destination. Lily was happy that they followed the right path, and she thanked the humble taxi driver for the ride. The end.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play outside with their bikes. One day, they see a big billboard on the road. The billboard has a picture of a shiny car and some words. Anna and Ben do not know what the words mean, but they think the car looks expensive.

"Wow, look at that car!" Anna says. "It is so pretty and red. I want to have a car like that when I grow up."

"Me too," Ben says. "But how can we get a car like that? We do not have a lot of money."

They think for a while. Then Ben has an idea. He says, "Maybe we can make our own car. We can use some cardboard and paint and glue. We can cut out the shape of the car and color it. Then we can stick it on our bikes and pretend we are driving."

Anna likes Ben's idea. She says, "That sounds fun. Let's do it. We can find some cardboard and paint and glue in the garage. Come on, let's go."

They run to the garage and look for the things they need. They find a big cardboard box, some scissors, some paint, and some glue. They also find some old magazines and newspapers. They start to cut out the shape of the car from the cardboard. They use the magazines and newspapers to make the windows and the wheels. They paint the car red and add some details. They are very proud of their work.

They stick the car on their bikes with some tape. They put on their helmets and get ready to ride. They say, "Look at us. We have a car like the billboard. We are so cool."

They ride their bikes with the car on the road. They wave to the people and the cars. They feel very happy. But then, a strong wind blows. The wind is so strong that it makes the car fly off their bikes. The car breaks into pieces and scatters on the road. Anna and Ben are shocked and sad. They stop their bikes and look at the mess.

"Oh no, our car!" Anna cries. "It is gone. It was so expensive."

"I know," Ben says. "It was our best car ever. We worked so hard on it. What can we do?"

They do not know what to do. They feel like crying. But then, they hear a voice. It is their mom. She has seen what happened. She comes to them and hugs them. She says, "I'm sorry, kids. Your car was very nice. But it was not very strong. The wind was too much for it. But don't worry. I have something for you."

She takes them to her car. She opens the trunk and shows them something. It is a toy car. It is red and shiny and has four wheels. It is not as big as the billboard car, but it is very cute. She says, "I saw this car in the store and I thought you would like it. It is a gift for you. You can play with it together. It is not expensive, but it is very fun."

Anna and Ben are surprised and happy. They say, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. We love you. And we love this car. It is our new car."

They hug their mom and take the toy car. They forget about the cardboard car. They play with the toy car on the sidewalk. They make noises and smile. They are happy again. The end.

"OK, I forgive you. But don't do it again." Mia said, smiling.

"Thank you, dolphin! You're so charming!" Mia said.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big box under a tree. It had a bow and a tag on it.

"Look, a surprise!" Lily said. "Maybe it is for us!"

Tom ran to the box and grabbed it. He wanted to open it and see what was inside. Lily ran after him and grabbed the other side of the box. She wanted to open it too.

"Let go, it is mine!" Tom shouted.

"No, it is mine!" Lily shouted back.

They pulled and tugged on the box. They did not see the man who was coming to the tree. He was the one who put the box there. It was a surprise for his son.

"Hey, what are you doing?" the man said in a loud voice. He was angry and scared. He thought the children were stealing his gift.

Tom and Lily dropped the box and looked at the man. They were afraid and sorry. They did not know it was his box.

"We are sorry, sir," Tom said.

"We thought it was a surprise for us," Lily said.

The man looked at them and sighed. He saw they were just curious and playful. He was not so angry anymore.

"It is okay, kids," he said. "But this box is not for you. It is for my son. He is having a birthday today. Do you want to say hello to him?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They followed the man to his son. He was playing with his friends. He was happy to see the box.

"Happy birthday, son!" the man said. "I have a surprise for you!"

He gave him the box and helped him open it. Inside was a toy train. The son smiled and hugged his dad.

"Thank you, dad! I love it!" he said.

He saw Tom and Lily and waved at them.

"Hi, I am Ben. Do you want to play with me?" he asked.

Tom and Lily smiled and nodded. They said sorry again and wished him a happy birthday. They became friends and played with the toy train. They had fun and learned to share.

Lily and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They also made snowballs and threw them at each other. They laughed and had fun.

Then Lily had an idea. She said to Ben, "Let's make snow angels!" Ben nodded and smiled. They lay down on the snow and moved their arms and legs. They made shapes like angels in the snow.

They got up and looked at their snow angels. They were very pretty. Lily said, "My snow angel is the best. She has a big dress and a halo." Ben said, "No, my snow angel is the best. He has wings and a sword."

They started to argue. They said, "Mine is better!" "No, mine is better!" They got angry and pushed each other.

Then they heard a voice. It was their mom. She said, "What are you doing? Stop fighting! You should share and be nice. Your snow angels are both beautiful. They are not expensive. They are free. You should be happy and grateful."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Ben." They hugged and said, "You are right, mom. Our snow angels are both beautiful. We are happy and grateful. We love you, mom. We love you, Lily. We love you, Ben."

They went back to playing in the snow. They spread more snow around and made more snow angels. They also made a snow dog and a snow cat. They had a lot of fun. They were happy and grateful.

Sam and Mia like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is the big train. The train has many cars that can attach to each other. They can make the train long or short, fast or slow.

One day, they find a new toy in their room. It is a soft animal. It has brown fur, four legs, and a long tail. It looks like a dog, but it is not a dog. It is a lion. Sam and Mia are curious. They want to play with the lion.

They take the lion to the train. They try to attach the lion to the train. But the lion does not fit. The lion is too big and too heavy. The train falls over. The lion roars. Sam and Mia are scared. They run away from the lion.

"Mommy, mommy, help!" they cry. "There is a lion in our room!"

Mommy hears them and comes to see. She sees the lion and the train. She smiles. She is not scared. She knows the lion is not real. It is a toy. She picks up the lion and hugs it.

"Don't worry, my loves," she says. "This is not a real lion. It is a gift from your uncle. He sent it to you from Africa. He works there and helps the real lions. He wanted you to have a safe animal to play with. Isn't it nice?"

Sam and Mia look at the lion. They see that it is soft and cuddly. They are not scared anymore. They smile. They hug the lion and thank mommy. They decide to give the lion a name. They call it Leo. They take Leo to their bed and snuggle with him. They are happy. They have a new friend.

Lila and Sam were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a new girl. She had brown skin and curly hair. Lila and Sam had white skin and straight hair.

"Who is she?" Lila asked Sam.

"I don't know. Let's talk to her," Sam said.

They walked to the new girl and said hello. The new girl smiled and said hello back. She told them her name was Zara and she was from another country.

"Wow, you are from another country? That is cool!" Sam said.

"Yes, it is. I like to learn new things and meet new people," Zara said.

Lila was confused. She did not understand why Zara had different skin and hair. She thought Zara was strange and did not belong.

"Lila, do you want to play with us?" Sam asked.

Lila shook her head. She did not want to play with Zara. She said she had to go home.

Sam was sad. He liked Zara and wanted to be friends with her. He said goodbye to Lila and stayed with Zara. They had fun playing in the park.

The next day, Lila came back to the park. She saw Sam and Zara playing again. She felt lonely and sorry. She realized she was wrong to judge Zara by her skin and hair. She wanted to be friends with her too.

She walked to Sam and Zara and said sorry. She said she was silly and rude. She said she wanted to play with them and learn from Zara.

Sam and Zara smiled and hugged Lila. They said they were happy to have her as a friend. They said they did not care about skin and hair. They cared about being kind and having fun.

Lila learned a lesson. She learned that people can be different and still be friends. She learned that skin and hair are not important. She learned that what matters is what is inside.

Lily and Tom were brother and sister. They liked to play in the attic. The attic had many old things, like toys, books and clothes. Lily and Tom liked to pretend they were pirates, or fairies, or explorers.

One day, they found a big box in the attic. They opened it and saw a shiny necklace. It had many colors and sparkles. Lily wanted to wear it. She said to Tom, "Can I have the necklace? It is so pretty. I will be a princess."

Tom said, "No, Lily. The necklace is not ours. It belongs to Mom. She told us not to touch her things. We have to be honest and put it back."

Lily did not listen to Tom. She said, "Mom will not know. She never comes to the attic. I will only wear it for a little while. Please, Tom, let me have it."

Tom did not want to fight with Lily. He said, "Okay, Lily. You can wear it. But you have to promise to put it back later. Do not forget, Lily. Do not forget."

Lily put on the necklace and smiled. She felt like a princess. She said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother. I will not forget. I will put it back later."

They played in the attic for a long time. They had fun. They forgot about the time. They forgot about Mom. They forgot about the necklace.

Mom came home from work. She went to the attic. She wanted to wear her necklace. It was a gift from her grandmother. It was very special to her. She looked for the box. She opened it. She saw that the necklace was gone. She was very angry and sad. She shouted, "Who took my necklace? Who did this?"

Lily and Tom heard Mom. They remembered the necklace. They felt scared and sorry. They ran to the attic. They said, "Mom, we are sorry. We took the necklace. We wanted to play with it. We forgot to put it back. Please, Mom, do not be mad."

Mom looked at Lily and Tom. She saw the necklace on Lily's neck. She said, "Lily, Tom, how could you do this? You lied to me. You stole from me. You broke my trust. You are not honest. You are not good. You are in big trouble."

Lily and Tom cried. They said, "Mom, we are sorry. We made a mistake. We love you. Please, Mom, forgive us."

Mom said, "No, Lily, Tom. I cannot forgive you. You have to learn your lesson. You have to give me back the necklace. You have to go to your rooms. You have to stay there for a long time. You have to think about what you did. You have to be sorry. You have to be honest. You have to be good."

Lily and Tom gave Mom back the necklace. They went to their rooms. They stayed there for a long time. They thought about what they did. They were sorry. They wanted to be honest. They wanted to be good. But Mom was still mad. She did not talk to them. She did not hug them. She did not love them. Lily and Tom were very sad. They wished they never found the necklace. They wished they never played in the attic. They wished they never forgot.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they find a big box in the garage. It has many buttons and lights. They are eager to see what it does.

"Can we test it?" Anna asks.

"OK, but be careful," Ben says. "It might be loud or hot."

They push some buttons and turn some knobs. The box makes a beep and a buzz. Then it is silent. They wait and look at the box.

"Maybe it is broken," Anna says.

"Or maybe it is doing something we can't see," Ben says.

They hear a voice from the box. It says, "Hello, Anna and Ben. I am a robot. Do you want to play with me?"

Anna and Ben are surprised and happy. They smile and clap.

"Yes, we do!" they say. "What is your name?"

The robot says, "My name is Rex. I can sing, dance, and tell jokes. Do you want to hear one?"

Anna and Ben nod. They are eager to hear a joke.

The robot says, "Why did the chicken cross the road?"

Anna and Ben think. They don't know.

The robot says, "To get to the other side!"

Anna and Ben laugh. They think the joke is funny.

They play with Rex for a long time. They have fun and learn new things. They are glad they tested the box. They make a new friend.

Lily ran to the box too. She saw a big train set with tracks and cars and bridges. It was the train set they had seen in the shop and wanted very much.

"It is our train set!" Lily said. "Thank you, thank you, thank you!"

They hugged each other and the box. They were very happy.

Tommy was watching them from the window. He was their neighbor and friend. He liked trains too. He wished he had a train set like that. He felt envious.

"Why do they get a train set and I don't?" Tommy said. He felt sad and angry.

He decided to go to the garden and join them. Maybe they would let him play with the train set too. He put on his shoes and coat and went outside.

"Hi, Lily, hi, Max!" Tommy said. "Can I play with you?"

Lily and Max smiled at him. They liked Tommy. He was a good friend.

"Sure, Tommy!" Lily said. "Come and see our train set! It is a gift from our grandma!"

They showed him the train set and how it worked. They let him hold the cars and the bridges. They made room for him on the grass.

Tommy felt happy. He forgot his envy. He thanked Lily and Max for sharing their train set. He said their grandma was very nice.

They played together for a long time. They made stories and noises and fun. They were very happy.

Lily liked to look at the birds in the park. She saw red birds, blue birds, yellow birds and more. She wished she had a bird of her own to play with. One day, she found a big birdcage in the trash. It was dirty and rusty, but Lily thought it was perfect. She took it home and put it in her room.

The next day, Lily went to the park again. She saw a small green bird on a branch. It was singing a pretty song. Lily wanted to make it her friend. She took out some bread from her pocket and threw it on the ground. The green bird flew down and ate the bread. Lily smiled and moved closer. She grabbed the bird and put it in the birdcage. She ran home with her new pet.

Lily was very happy with her green bird. She named it Kiwi and gave it water and seeds. She talked to it and sang to it. She thought Kiwi liked her too. But Kiwi was not happy. He missed his home and his friends. He wanted to fly and be free. He looked for a way to escape the birdcage.

One night, Lily forgot to close the door of the birdcage. Kiwi saw his chance. He pushed the door open and flew out. He flew out of the window and into the dark sky. He was free again. He did not look back.

The next morning, Lily woke up and went to see Kiwi. But Kiwi was not there. The birdcage was empty. Lily was sad and confused. She did not understand where Kiwi went. She looked everywhere, but she could not find him. She cried and cried. She wished she had never taken Kiwi from the park. She learned a hard lesson. You cannot keep a wild bird in a cage.

They walk to the park with their moms. They find a nice spot under a big tree. They lay a blanket on the grass. They open their sack and take out their food and drinks. They share their sandwiches, apples, and juice. They say, "Yum, yum, this is good!"

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they find a big book with many pictures. The book is about animals and plants.

"Look, Sam, this is a cell," Mia says, pointing to a small circle. "It is very tiny. You need a glass to see it."

"What is a cell?" Sam asks, curious.

"A cell is a part of everything that is alive. You have cells, I have cells, the dog has cells, the flower has cells. Cells make us grow and be healthy," Mia explains.

"Wow, that is amazing. Can we eat cells?" Sam wonders.

Mia laughs. "No, silly, we cannot eat cells. We eat food that has cells, like bread and fruit and cheese. But we cannot see the cells in the food. They are too small."

Sam nods. He understands. He likes to eat food that has cells. He thinks it is lovely.

"Can I have some of your cheese, Mia?" he asks.

"Sure, Sam, you can have some of my cheese. It is yummy. Here you go," Mia says, sharing her snack.

They eat the cheese and look at the book. They learn more about cells and other things. They are happy. They are friends.

Lily was a curious girl who liked to explore the garden. One day, she saw a small hole in the ground. She wondered what was inside. She knelt down and peered into the hole.

"Hello, is anyone there?" she asked.

A tiny voice answered, "Yes, I am here. I am a mole. Who are you?"

Lily was surprised and happy. She had never seen a mole before. She said, "I am Lily. I am a girl. Can I see you?"

The mole said, "Maybe, but you have to be very quiet and gentle. I am shy and scared of loud noises and big things."

Lily nodded and said, "OK, I will be quiet and gentle. Can you come out of the hole?"

The mole said, "I don't know. I have never come out of the hole. It is dark and safe here. Out there, it is bright and scary. There are birds and cats and dogs that want to eat me."

Lily said, "But I won't let them eat you. I will protect you. And you can see the flowers and the trees and the sky. They are beautiful. Don't you want to see them?"

The mole thought for a moment. He was curious too. He said, "Maybe, but only for a little bit. And you have to hold my paw and stay close to me."

Lily said, "OK, I will hold your paw and stay close to you. Come on, let's go."

The mole dared to come out of the hole. He felt the sun on his fur and the breeze on his nose. He saw the colors and shapes of the garden. He was amazed and happy. He said, "Wow, this is wonderful. Thank you, Lily, for showing me this."

Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, mole. I'm glad you like it. You are my new friend."

The mole smiled and said, "You are my new friend too, Lily. But can we go back to the hole soon? I miss my home."

Lily said, "Of course, we can go back to the hole soon. But can we play again tomorrow?"

The mole said, "Yes, we can play again tomorrow. But only if you are quiet and gentle."

Lily said, "I will be quiet and gentle. I promise."

They hugged and went back to the hole. They said goodbye and goodnight. They were happy and curious friends.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the bathroom. They liked to turn on the faucet and make bubbles with the soap. They also liked to splash water on each other and laugh.

One day, their mom told them to stop playing with the faucet and go to bed. She said they were wasting water and making a mess. Tim and Kim did not listen to their mom. They were ignorant. They thought they knew better than their mom.

They kept playing with the faucet and the soap. They did not see that the water was overflowing from the sink. They did not hear that their mom was calling them. They did not notice that the floor was wet and slippery.

Suddenly, Tim slipped on the wet floor and hit his head on the toilet. He cried out loud. Kim got scared and ran to help him. She also slipped on the wet floor and fell down. She hurt her knee and elbow. She cried too.

Their mom heard their cries and ran to the bathroom. She saw the water, the soap, and the twins on the floor. She was angry and worried. She turned off the faucet and dried the twins with a towel. She checked their wounds and put band-aids on them. She hugged them and said, "You should have listened to me. Playing with the faucet is dangerous and wasteful. You were ignorant and naughty. Now you are hurt and sorry. Next time, do what I say and go to bed when I tell you. OK?"

Tim and Kim nodded and said, "OK, mom. We are sorry. We love you." They learned their lesson and never played with the faucet again.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big barrel near the farm. They wondered what was inside it.

"Let's open it and see," said Tim, who was older and braver.

"No, we should not," said Sam, who was younger and obedient. "Mom said we should not touch things that are not ours."

But Tim did not listen to Sam. He climbed on the barrel and tried to lift the lid. He pulled and pulled, but the lid was too heavy. He asked Sam to help him.

"Please, Sam, help me open it. Maybe there is something fun inside," he said.

Sam did not want to disobey his brother, so he climbed on the barrel too. He pushed and pushed, but the lid was still too heavy. They both tried harder and harder, until they heard a loud pop.

The lid flew off the barrel and hit them on the head. They fell off the barrel and landed on the ground. They felt dizzy and sore. They looked at the barrel and saw a lot of white powder coming out of it.

They did not know what it was, but it smelled bad and made them sneeze. They sneezed and sneezed, until they could not breathe. They tried to get up and run away, but they were too weak and sick.

They lay on the ground, covered in white powder, and cried for help. But no one heard them. No one came to save them. They had opened the farmer's barrel of fertilizer, and it was poisonous. They had made a big mistake, and they paid a big price. They never played outside again.

Sara and Ben came back to the bench. They looked for their treasure jar. They could not find it. They asked their friends if they saw it. They said no. They looked around the park. They could not see it. They felt scared and angry. They had lost their treasure jar.

They saw the mean boy across the street. He had their treasure jar. He was laughing and shaking it. He did not see the car coming. The car hit him. He dropped the treasure jar. It broke into pieces. The water, sand, stones, and bugs spilled out. The mean boy cried. Sara and Ben cried. They had lost their treasure jar forever.

One day, Lily and Tom went to the park with their mom. They saw a big bush with many blueberries on it. Lily and Tom loved blueberries, so they ran to the bush and picked some.

"Look, mom, we found blueberries!" they said.

Mom smiled and said, "That's nice, but be careful. Some blueberries might be bad. They might be sour or have bugs in them. You should always notice how they look and smell before you eat them."

Lily and Tom nodded, but they were too excited to listen. They put some blueberries in their mouths and chewed. Some were sweet and juicy, but some were bad. They made their faces twist and their tongues hurt.

"Yuck, these blueberries are bad!" they said, spitting them out.

Mom came over and said, "I told you to notice how they look and smell. See, these bad blueberries are wrinkled and brown. They are old and rotten. You should only eat the blueberries that are round and blue. They are fresh and tasty."

Lily and Tom felt sorry and said, "We're sorry, mom. We didn't notice. We were too greedy. We will be more careful next time."

Mom hugged them and said, "It's okay, my loves. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Now, let's wash our hands and find some good blueberries to enjoy."

Lily and Tom smiled and said, "Yes, mom. Thank you, mom. We love you, mom."

The moral of the story is: You should always notice what you eat and not be greedy. Bad food can make you sick and unhappy. Good food can make you healthy and happy.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. They also had a dog named Spot who was very friendly and liked to chase balls.

One day, they saw a giant walking on the street. He was taller than their house and had a long beard and a big hat. He looked scary and angry. He stomped his feet and made loud noises.

"Who is that?" Anna asked Ben.

"I don't know. Maybe he is lost. He is not normal," Ben said.

"Let's hide behind the slide. Maybe he will go away," Anna said.

They ran to the slide and crouched behind it. Spot followed them and barked at the giant.

"Shh, Spot. Behave. You will make him see us," Ben whispered.

The giant heard Spot and turned his head. He saw the twins and the dog behind the slide. He smiled and walked towards them.

"Hello, little ones. Don't be afraid. I am not here to hurt you. I am just looking for my friend. Have you seen him?" the giant asked.

He had a deep and gentle voice. He bent down and reached out his hand.

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They were still scared, but they also felt curious. They decided to be brave and talk to the giant.

"Who is your friend?" Anna asked.

"He is a dragon. He is green and has wings and breathes fire. He flew away from our home and I can't find him. He likes to play with me and make jokes. He is very nice," the giant said.

"A dragon? Wow, that sounds cool. We have never seen a dragon. Where is your home?" Ben asked.

"Our home is far away, in the mountains. We live in a cave with other giants and dragons. We have a lot of fun there. But sometimes we like to explore new places and meet new people. That's why we came here. But we got separated and I don't know where he is. I miss him very much," the giant said.

He looked sad and lonely. Anna and Ben felt sorry for him. They wanted to help him.

"Maybe we can help you find your friend. We know this place very well. We can ask around and see if anyone has seen a dragon. Maybe he is hiding somewhere. What is his name?" Anna said.

"His name is Sparky. He likes shiny things and loud noises. He is very smart and playful. He is my best friend," the giant said.

He smiled and thanked the twins. He picked them up and put them on his shoulders. Spot jumped and licked his face. The giant laughed and petted him.

They walked together on the street, looking for Sparky. They asked the people they met, but no one had seen a dragon. They checked the park, the school, the store, but no sign of Sparky. They were starting to lose hope.

Then they heard a loud roar and saw a flash of fire. They looked up and saw a green dragon flying in the sky. He had a big grin and a shiny necklace around his neck. He saw the giant and the twins and waved his claws.

"Sparky!" the giant shouted.

He ran towards him and hugged him. The dragon hugged him back and licked his face. He looked at the twins and smiled.

"Hello, little ones. You must be the giant's new friends. Thank you for helping him find me. I was just having some fun. I found this pretty necklace in a dumpster and I wanted to show it to him. But I got lost and I couldn't find him. I was worried and sad. I'm sorry for making trouble," Sparky said.

He had a high and squeaky voice. He sounded sorry and happy.

"It's okay, Sparky. I'm glad you're safe. I was worried and sad too. I'm happy to see you. And these are Anna and Ben. They are very nice and brave. They helped me look for you. They are my new friends too," the giant said.

He introduced the twins and the dragon. They all became friends and played together. They had a lot of fun. They shared stories and jokes and games. They forgot about their differences and enjoyed their similarities.

They learned that being normal is not important. Being kind and friendly is. They learned that being different is not scary. Being curious and open is. They learned that being big or small is not a problem. Being helpful and respectful is.

They learned that being friends is the best thing in the world.

"Okay, Lily, let's sail back. But first, let's take this rock with us. It can be our treasure," Tom said, putting the rock in his pocket.

They got back on the boat and sailed across the pond. They waved to their mom, who was watching them from a bench. They had fun sailing and exploring, but they were happy to be home.

The birds were very alert now and knew to be careful around the cat. They did not want to be eaten too. The little bird was gone forever, but the other birds would always remember it and sing songs in its memory.

After finishing his snack, Timmy asked his mommy if they could go to the library. His mommy said yes and they went to the library together. Timmy was so happy to be surrounded by all the books he loved. He even found a new book that he couldn't wait to take home and read. 

After spending some time at the library, Timmy and his mommy went back home. Timmy snuggled up with his new book and enjoyed his yummy snack. He felt so lucky to have such a great day filled with his favorite things.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety was bald, which means he didn't have any feathers on his head. He lived in a big tree with his friend, a squirrel named Nutty.

One day, Tweety and Nutty were playing hide and seek. Nutty climbed up the tree to hide, but he accidentally split the branch he was on. "Oh no!" cried Nutty. "I'm falling!"

Tweety quickly flew over and caught Nutty in his beak. "Phew, that was a close one," said Nutty. "Thanks for saving me, Tweety."

From that day on, Tweety and Nutty played quietly in the tree, making sure not to split any more branches. They knew that they needed to be careful so that they could stay safe and happy together.

After pruning the bushes, Timmy realized that he had been selfish with his toy earlier. He felt bad and decided to share it with his friend. Timmy's friend was happy and they had fun playing together.

Timmy learned that it's important to share and be kind to others. He also realized that sometimes doing things we don't want to do, like pruning the bushes, can make things better in the end. And that's the moral of the story!

Mommy hugged Timmy and said, "Don't worry, Timmy. Ghosts aren't real. It was probably just a noise from outside." 

Timmy felt better and went back to playing with his toys. He was happy to know that ghosts weren't real and that he was safe with his mommy.

Mommy looked up and saw that it was just a toy monkey on a string. They both laughed and went back to watching the kids play. The cop car drove away, but Lily would always remember the nice cop who waved at her. The end.

Anna loved to draw with her pencil. She drew many things: flowers, animals, houses, people. She was gifted at drawing. She could make her pictures look real and beautiful. She wanted to share her drawings with others.

One day, she went to a new school. She was nervous and shy. She did not know anyone there. She brought her pencil and some paper with her. She hoped to make some friends.

At recess, she saw a group of kids playing with a ball. She wanted to join them, but she was afraid they would not like her. She sat on a bench and started to draw. She drew the kids, the ball, the trees, the sky.

A boy named Ben saw her drawing. He was curious and friendly. He walked over to her and said, "Hi, I'm Ben. What are you drawing?"

Anna looked up and saw his smile. She felt a little less nervous. She said, "Hi, I'm Anna. I'm drawing you and the others."

Ben looked at her drawing and was amazed. He said, "Wow, you are gifted at drawing. You made us look so real and happy. Can I see more of your drawings?"

Anna nodded and showed him her paper. She had many drawings of different things. Ben liked them all. He said, "You are very talented. Do you want to play with us? We can share the ball."

Anna smiled and said, "Yes, I would like that. Thank you for being nice to me."

Ben said, "You're welcome. Come on, let's go. I'll introduce you to the others. They will like you too."

He took her hand and led her to the group. He said, "Hey, everyone, this is Anna. She is new here. She is gifted at drawing. Look at her pictures."

The other kids looked at her pictures and were impressed. They said, "Wow, those are awesome. You are very good at drawing. Welcome to our school. Do you want to play with us?"

Anna felt happy and accepted. She said, "Yes, I do. Thank you for welcoming me."

She put her pencil and paper in her backpack and joined the game. She had fun playing with the ball and making new friends. She was glad she came to the new school. She was glad she met Ben. She was glad she had her pencil.

Mia and Leo are playing in the park. They see a big slide with colorful steps. Mia wants to go on the slide, but Leo is scared.

"Come on, Leo, let's go on the slide. It looks fun!" Mia says.

"No, no, no. I don't want to go on the slide. It is too high and too fast. I am scared." Leo says.

Mia tries to make Leo feel brave. She says, "Don't be scared, Leo. I will go with you. We can hold hands and slide together. It will be fun, I promise."

But Leo refuses to go on the slide. He shakes his head and says, "No, no, no. I don't want to go on the slide. You can go by yourself. I will wait here."

Mia is sad. She wants to play with Leo, but she also wants to go on the slide. She decides to go on the slide by herself. She climbs the colorful steps and sits on the slide. She says, "Bye, Leo. I will see you soon."

She slides down the slide and feels the wind in her hair. She laughs and says, "Whee! This is fun!"

She gets off the slide and looks for Leo. But Leo is not where she left him. She is worried. She starts to search for Leo. She looks behind the trees, under the benches, and in the sandbox. She does not see Leo.

She calls out, "Leo, where are you? Leo, come out, please!"

She hears a voice from behind the slide. It is Leo. He says, "Here I am, Mia. I am sorry. I was hiding. I was scared."

Mia runs to Leo and hugs him. She says, "I am glad you are okay, Leo. I was looking for you. I was worried. Why were you hiding?"

Leo says, "I was hiding because I was scared. I saw you go on the slide and you looked so happy. I wanted to go on the slide too, but I was still scared. I was afraid you would not play with me anymore. I was afraid you would not be my friend anymore."

Mia says, "Oh, Leo, that is silly. I will always play with you. I will always be your friend. I like the slide, but I like you more. You don't have to go on the slide if you don't want to. We can play something else. We can play with the ball, or the swings, or the seesaw. What do you want to play?"

Leo smiles and says, "I want to play with you, Mia. You are my best friend. Maybe next time I will try the slide. But only if you hold my hand."

Mia says, "Okay, Leo. I will hold your hand. And I will always be your friend. Come on, let's play!"

They hold hands and run to the swings. They laugh and play and have fun. They are happy.

Tom and Sam were friends who liked to joke a lot. They liked to joke with each other and with other kids. One day, they saw a big boat on the lake. They wanted to go on the boat and have fun.

They asked the man who owned the boat if they could go on it. The man said yes, but only if they were careful and did not joke on the boat. He said the boat was not a toy and could be dangerous. Tom and Sam said they understood and thanked the man.

They went on the boat and looked around. They saw many things on the boat, like ropes, nets, hooks, and fish. They thought they were very cool. But they also saw a sign that said "Do not touch". They wondered what was behind the sign.

Tom had an idea. He said to Sam, "Let's joke with the man. Let's touch the sign and see what happens. It will be funny." Sam was not sure. He said, "But the man said not to joke on the boat. He said it could be dangerous. Maybe we should listen to him." Tom said, "Don't be scared. It's just a joke. Come on, it will be fun."

Tom and Sam went to the sign and touched it. As soon as they did, they heard a loud noise. The sign was a button that made the boat go very fast. The boat started to move on the lake, and Tom and Sam were scared. They did not know how to stop the boat. They screamed for help.

The man who owned the boat heard them and ran to the boat. He was angry and worried. He jumped on the boat and stopped it. He said to Tom and Sam, "What did you do? Why did you touch the sign? I told you not to joke on the boat. You could have hurt yourselves or others. You were very naughty and foolish."

Tom and Sam felt sorry and ashamed. They said they were sorry and that they did not mean to cause trouble. They said they just wanted to joke and have fun. The man said, "Joking is good, but not when it is dangerous or disrespectful. You have to be careful and responsible when you are on a boat or anywhere else. You have to respect the rules and the people who own the things. You have to learn from your mistake and never do it again."

Tom and Sam said they understood and that they would never do it again. They apologized to the man again and thanked him for letting them go on the boat. They learned their lesson and never joked on a boat again. They also learned to joke in a nice and safe way with each other and with other kids. They were still friends who liked to joke a lot, but they were also friends who knew how to be careful and respectful.
