One day, Lily saw her mom's makeup bag on the bed. She wanted to play with it, but her mom was not home. She was at work. Lily thought she could play with it for a little while and put it back before her mom came back.

She took the makeup bag and went to her room. She opened it and saw many colors and brushes. She started to put some on her face. She felt happy and pretty.

But then she heard a noise. It was her brother, Max. He was coming to her room. He was noisy and loud. He liked to tease her and make her cry.

He opened the door and saw Lily with the makeup. He laughed and said, "You look funny! You look like a clown! Mom will be mad at you!"

Lily felt scared and sad. She did not like what Max said. She wanted him to go away. She said, "No, I don't! I look like a princess! Go away, Max! Leave me alone!"

Max did not go away. He came closer and tried to take the makeup bag from her. He said, "Give me that! You are not supposed to play with mom's makeup! I will tell her what you did!"

Lily did not want to give him the makeup bag. She held it tight and said, "No, don't! It's mine! I will put it back! Don't tell mom!"

They started to pull and push. The makeup bag was in the middle. They were both strong and stubborn. They did not want to let go.

But then something happened. The makeup bag ripped. The colors and brushes fell out. They flew in the air and landed on the floor, on the bed, on the wall. Some of them broke and made a mess.

Lily and Max stopped fighting. They looked at the makeup. They looked at each other. They looked at the door. They heard a sound. It was their mom. She was home. She was coming to their room.

They felt sorry and scared. They knew they were in trouble. They did not know what to say. They wished they had not fought. They wished they had not played with the makeup. They wished they had hung it back on the bed.

Sam and Lily were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big red slide. They wanted to go on it.

"Can we do it, please?" Sam asked his mom.

"OK, but be careful. The slide is very high and fast," his mom said.

Sam and Lily ran to the slide. They waited for their turn. Then they climbed up the ladder. Sam went first. He sat on the slide and pushed himself down. He felt the wind in his hair and the sun on his face. He laughed and shouted, "Whee!"

Lily saw Sam having fun. She wanted to do it too. She sat on the slide and pushed herself down. But she did not laugh or shout. She felt something scratch her leg. She looked down and saw a big bee. The bee was angry. It stung Lily on her leg. Lily screamed and cried. She fell off the slide and hit the ground.

Sam heard Lily scream and cry. He ran to her and saw the bee and the sting. He felt sorry for Lily. He tried to help her. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will get your mom. She will make it better."

But Lily's mom was not there. She had gone to the bathroom. She did not hear Lily scream and cry. She did not see Lily fall and hurt. She did not know Lily had a bee sting. She did not know Lily was allergic to bees.

Lily's leg started to swell and itch. She felt sick and dizzy. She could not breathe well. She needed help. But no one came. Lily closed her eyes and fainted.

The end.

Tom and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were lions and chase each other. They wore pants with stripes and spots to look like lions. They also made loud roars to scare the birds and the squirrels.

"Roar! I'm going to catch you, Mia!" Tom said, running after his sister.

"Roar! You can't catch me, Tom! I'm too fast!" Mia said, dodging behind a tree.

They ran and roared and had fun. But they did not see the big dog that was watching them from the other side of the park. The dog did not like their roars. He thought they were trying to take his bone. He growled and barked and ran towards them.

Tom and Mia heard the dog and stopped playing. They saw the dog and felt worried. He was much bigger and louder than them. He looked angry and hungry. They did not know what to do.

"Help! Help!" Tom and Mia shouted, holding each other.

The dog came closer and closer. He opened his mouth and showed his teeth. He was ready to bite them.

But then, they heard another roar. A louder and stronger roar. A roar that made the dog stop and run away. A roar that came from their mom.

"Mom!" Tom and Mia cried, running to her.

"Are you okay, my little lions?" Mom asked, hugging them.

"Yes, Mom, we're okay. Thank you for saving us!" Tom and Mia said.

Mom smiled and kissed them. She was wearing pants with flowers and a shirt with a lion. She had heard their roars and came to see what was going on. She saw the dog and scared him away with her roar.

"Let's go home, my little lions. It's time for lunch. And don't worry, the dog won't bother you again. He knows who's the boss here." Mom said, leading them to the car.

"Roar!" Tom and Mia said, feeling happy and safe. They liked to pretend they were lions, but they loved their mom more. She was the best lion of all.

One day, Lily's mom made a big pot of soup for dinner. She put in carrots, potatoes, onions, and cauliflower. Lily did not like cauliflower. She thought it was white and boring and yucky. She wanted to skip her soup and eat something else.

"Mom, can I have a sandwich instead of soup?" Lily asked.

"No, Lily, you have to eat your soup. It is good for you and it has many vegetables. Cauliflower is one of them. It is not boring, it is crunchy and tasty. Try it, you might like it," Mom said.

Lily made a face and pushed her bowl away. She did not want to try it. She wanted to skip it.

Mom sighed and had an idea. She took out some food coloring and added a few drops to Lily's soup. She stirred it and showed it to Lily.

"Look, Lily, your soup is pink now. Pink is your favorite color. Do you want to try it now?" Mom asked.

Lily looked at her soup. It was pink and pretty. She liked pink. She was curious. She took a spoon and tasted it. It was warm and creamy and sweet. She liked it. She ate some more. She found a piece of cauliflower and bit it. It was crunchy and tasty. She liked it too. She ate all her soup and smiled.

"Mom, I like pink soup. And I like cauliflower. Thank you for making it for me," Lily said.

Mom hugged her and smiled too.

"You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you liked it. You see, sometimes you have to try new things before you decide if you like them or not. You might be surprised by what you find. That is a good lesson to learn," Mom said.

Lily nodded and agreed. She learned something new today. She was happy and proud. She skipped to her room to play. She was still Lily the Skipper, but now she was also Lily the Soup Lover.

"No, they are mine, teacher! Ben grabbed them from me!" Lily said.

"Listen, Lily and Ben, fighting is not nice. It hurts your feelings and it hurts the crayons. There are enough crayons for everyone, and you can take turns to use them. Why don't you settle this by saying sorry to each other and sharing the desk and the crayons?" she suggested.

Lily and Ben looked at each other and felt a little ashamed. They knew the teacher was right and they did not want to be mean to each other. They nodded and said sorry to each other.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I should have let you use some of the crayons," Ben said.

"Uh-oh!" Tim says. "This is loose!"

"Hi, Tim and Liz!" Ben says. "Do you want to play with me?"

"Yes, please!" Tim and Liz say. "But we can't attach our shoes!"

Ben smiles. He comes to them. He helps them attach their shoes.

"Look!" Ben says. "This is how you do it. You put the strap on the buckle. Then, you press it. Click! It fits. You put the lace through the hole. Then, you cross it. You loop it. You pull it. Ta-da! It stays."

"Wow!" Tim and Liz say. "You are so smart!"

"Thank you, Ben!" Tim and Liz say. "You are so kind!"

"You're welcome, Tim and Liz!" Ben says. "Now, let's go to the park!"

She took the stick from Timmy. She hugged him. She helped him back to his crib. She covered him with a blanket. She sang him a song. Timmy felt sorry. He said sorry to his sister and his crib. He closed his eyes. He fell asleep. He dreamed of a bed. But he also dreamed of his crib. He loved his crib too.

Ben was a boy who liked to play with bricks. He had many bricks of different colors and shapes. He could build houses, towers, cars and animals with his bricks. He was very proud of his bricks and did not like to share them with anyone.

One day, a new girl came to his school. Her name was Mia. She had no bricks at home. She only had a few old toys that were broken or dirty. She was very humble and kind. She wanted to make friends with Ben and play with his bricks.

But Ben did not want to play with Mia. He thought she was poor and dirty. He said, "Go away, Mia. You cannot touch my bricks. They are mine. You have nothing to play with. You are not my friend."

Mia felt very sad and lonely. She did not understand why Ben was so mean to her. She did not want to take his bricks. She only wanted to play with him and have fun.

One day, Ben was playing with his bricks in the playground. He had built a big tower that reached the sky. He was very happy and proud of his tower. He said, "Look at my tower. It is the best tower in the world. No one can make a tower like mine."

But then, a strong wind came and blew his tower down. His bricks fell to the ground and broke into pieces. Ben was very sad and angry. He cried, "No, no, no. My tower, my bricks. They are ruined. What will I do now?"

He looked around and saw Mia. She was sitting on a bench with a few of her old toys. She saw Ben's tower fall and his bricks break. She felt sorry for him. She said, "Ben, are you okay? Do you want to play with me? I have some toys that you can use. They are not much, but they are fun."

Ben looked at Mia and her toys. He felt ashamed of how he had treated her. He realized that she was a good and generous person. He said, "Mia, I am sorry. I was very rude and selfish to you. I did not want to share my bricks with you. I thought I was better than you. But I was wrong. You are a better friend than me. You are humble and kind. You offered to share your toys with me when I had nothing. Can you forgive me? Can we be friends?"

Mia smiled and said, "Of course, Ben. I forgive you. We can be friends. Come, let's play together. We can use your bricks and my toys. We can make something new and beautiful."

Ben and Mia played together and had a lot of fun. They used their bricks and toys to make a house, a car, an animal and a flower. They were happy and proud of their creations. They learned to share and care for each other. They became the best of friends.

The moral of the story is: Do not judge people by what they have or do not have. Be humble and kind to everyone. Share what you have and you will find happiness and friendship.

"Sure, Lily. How do you use it?" Ben asked.

Lily showed Ben how to put a slide under the microscope and adjust the knobs. She gave him a slide with a bug on it.

"Look, Ben. This is a bug. Can you see it?" Lily asked.

Ben looked through the microscope and gasped. He saw the bug's eyes, legs, wings, and antennae. He saw how hairy and colorful it was.

"Wow, Lily. That's amazing. The bug looks so different. Can I see another slide?" Ben asked.

Lily nodded and gave him another slide with a leaf on it. Ben looked through the microscope and saw the veins, cells, and spots on the leaf. He was amazed by the details and colors.

"Lily, this is so cool. Thank you for showing me. Can I show you something too?" Ben asked.

Lily smiled and said, "Sure, Ben. What do you want to show me?"

"Sure, you can ride the motorcycle. But only in the driveway. And you have to wear helmets and jackets. It is cold outside," Dad says.

He gives them helmets and jackets. They are warm and fuzzy. Lily and Sam put them on. They say thank you to Dad. They run back to the garage. They climb on the motorcycle. Lily sits in front. Sam sits behind. They hold on tight.

Dad comes to the garage. He starts the motorcycle. It makes a loud noise. Lily and Sam giggle. They feel the motorcycle move. Dad pushes a button. The motorcycle zips forward. Lily and Sam scream with joy. They zip up and down the driveway. They feel the wind in their faces. They have fun. They love the motorcycle.

Tom and Sam were friends. They liked to play with toys and books. One day, they found a big map on the wall. The map had many colors and shapes. Tom pointed at a red shape and said, "This is my nation. It is the best nation in the world."

Sam looked at the map and saw a blue shape next to the red one. He said, "No, this is my nation. It is the best nation in the world. Your nation is bad and small."

Tom and Sam started to argue. They both wanted to touch their nation on the map. They pushed and pulled each other. They did not listen to each other. They did not share.

The map was old and thin. It could not hold Tom and Sam's weight. It ripped and fell off the wall. The colors and shapes were gone. Tom and Sam looked at the map and cried. They had broken the map. They had no nation.

The teacher heard the noise and came to the room. She saw the map on the floor and the boys crying. She was very angry. She said, "What have you done? You have ruined the map. You have been bad and selfish. You have to go to the corner and think about what you did. You have no friends."

They asked their friend, who was also a kind person, and they explained that some vegetables are bitter but still good for you. 

The first person decided to try the bitter vegetable again and found that they liked it. They wondered why they didn't like it before. From that day on, they grew more bitter vegetables in their garden and shared them with their friends. Everyone was happy and healthy eating the bitter vegetables. The end.

Lily's friend Timmy said, "I saw a boy take the water bottles and run away." Lily felt upset because they were all so thirsty. But then she remembered that her mom had also packed some warm juice boxes in the cooler. They weren't as refreshing as the cold water, but they were still tasty and helped quench their thirst. 

Lily and her friends continued to play, and even though they didn't have cold water, they were happy to have something to drink. And Lily felt proud of herself for remembering the warm juice boxes in the cooler.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to explore the world around him. One day, he went on a walk with his mom and they saw a cute bunny. Timmy said, "Look, Mommy, a cute bunny!" His mom replied, "Yes, it is very cute." 

Timmy wanted to examine the bunny, so he asked his mom if he could get closer. His mom said yes and Timmy slowly walked towards the bunny. The bunny hopped away to the east, but Timmy followed it. 

When Timmy finally caught up to the bunny, he saw that it had a little carrot in its mouth. Timmy said, "Hello, Mr. Bunny, can I have some of your carrot?" The bunny didn't answer, but Timmy took that as a yes and took a bite. It was very yummy! Timmy and his mom continued their walk, happy to have made a new furry friend. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a ship sailing on the big blue sea. The ship had many people on it, including a thoughtful captain who always made sure everyone was safe.

One day, the ship encountered a storm. The waves were big and the wind was strong. The captain tried his best to steer the ship, but it was too difficult. The ship was going to sink!

But then, the captain had an idea. He told everyone to tie themselves to the mast, which is a big pole on the ship. They all did as he said, and the ship rode out the storm. In the end, everyone was safe.

The moral of the story is that if you listen to wise and thoughtful people, you can overcome any problem. And sometimes, even the scariest situations can have a happy ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her friend Timmy were playing outside in the snow. They saw a big igloo made of snow. "Wow, that's so cool!" said Lily. "Let's go inside!" 

But when they got inside, they saw that it was very dirty. "Eww, this igloo is so dirty!" said Timmy. "We need to clean it." So they started to clean the igloo. They used their hands to scoop out the dirty snow and throw it outside. 

After a while, the igloo was clean and shiny. "Look, it's like a brand new igloo!" said Lily. But then they heard a voice. "Hey, what are you doing in my igloo?" It was a polar bear. "Oh no, we're sorry! We didn't know it was yours," said Timmy. "It's okay," said the polar bear. "But this igloo is fake. I made it out of plastic." 

Lily and Timmy were surprised. "Fake? What does that mean?" asked Lily. "It means it's not real. It's just pretend," said the polar bear. "Oh, okay," said Lily. "Well, it was still fun to clean it!"

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He was three years old and loved to explore. One day he saw some mud and he wanted to touch it. He walked over and squished his hands in the mud. It felt slimy and he smiled. He started playing with it and made a mud castle. 

He heard his mom calling him and wanted to come back but he didn't want to leave the mud behind. So, he picked up a handful of mud and put it in his pocket. He started walking back home. 

As he was walking, he passed a puddle. He took the mud out of his pocket and looked at it. Suddenly, he felt bad and ashamed. He didn't want to get in trouble for taking the mud without asking, so he quickly threw the mud back into the puddle. He smiled, feeling better. 

He kept walking happily back home, ready to tell his mom all about the mud he found.

Once there was a tall tree in the forest. Every day, a squirrel climbed to the top most branches and nibbled on the nuts. One day, a whip fell from the sky and stuck in the branches.

The squirrel was curious and started to pull the whip. Suddenly, it started to spin and the tree began to move! Its roots started to rot and the tree started to move around the forest.

The squirrel saw the tall trees move and was very excited. He jumped and hopped on the branches as the trees swayed around the forest.

The squirrel loved his new adventure and would often grab the whip and continue spinning around the forest whenever he felt like it!

The big bear was surprised. Then it growled and walked away.

The little girl was so surprised that she just stayed quiet. 
The little bear stayed with her until she was ready to go home. 
Then the brave little girl thanked her new friend and said goodbye. 

After that, the little girl walked home safely. 
She never forgot how brave the little bear was and how it saved her from the big bear's threat.

The bear felt very sorry for the bluebird, so he decided to help her. He brought the bluebird back to his home and he took care of her very well. He made a soft bed for her with leaves, and he gave her lots of food and water. Little by little, the bluebird started to feel better. 

The bluebird and the bear became great friends. They spent every day together playing and having fun in the forest. The bear was no longer lonely, and the bluebird was happy to have a friend. They were so glad that their friendship had helped them both feel better.

They filled the tub with water and got in. They took turns to scoop some food and splash it in the water. They made a big mess, but they had a lot of fun. They pretended they were chefs and made creative dishes with the food. They used carrots as boats, peas as bubbles, and cheese as stars.

Their mom heard the noise and came to see what they were doing. She was not happy. She saw the food and the water all over the floor and the walls. She told them to get out of the tub and clean up.

Lily and Max were sorry. They did not mean to make mom angry. They helped her to wipe the food and the water. They said they were sorry and gave her a hug. They promised to not splash food again. Mom smiled and gave them a kiss. She said she loved them, but they had to be more careful. She said they could be creative in other ways, like drawing or singing. Lily and Max agreed. They were hungry and tired. They ate their lunch and took a nap. They dreamed of new and fun things to do.

Jenny was a little girl who liked to visit her grandma every week. Grandma was elderly and lived in a small house with a garden. Jenny loved to help grandma water the flowers and feed the birds. Grandma always had cookies and stories for Jenny.

One day, Jenny and grandma were sitting on the couch, reading a book about a princess and a dragon. Jenny was very curious and asked grandma many questions. Grandma smiled and answered them all. She was happy to see Jenny so interested.

"Grandma, can I go to the toilet?" Jenny asked after a while.

"Of course, dear. You know where it is, right?" Grandma said.

"Yes, grandma. It's next to your bedroom." Jenny said. She got up and walked to the toilet.

But when she opened the door, she saw something that scared her. There was a big spider on the wall, near the sink. It had eight hairy legs and two shiny eyes. Jenny screamed and ran back to the couch.

"Grandma, grandma, there's a spider in the toilet!" Jenny cried.

"Oh, no, Jenny. Don't be afraid. It's just a little spider. It won't hurt you." Grandma said. She got up and took Jenny's hand. "Come on, let's go and see."

Grandma and Jenny walked to the toilet. Grandma turned on the light and pointed to the spider.

"See, Jenny? It's not so big. It's just a little friend who likes to live in the toilet. He helps us by eating the flies and the bugs. He's not scary at all." Grandma said.

"Really, grandma?" Jenny asked.

"Really, Jenny. He's harmless. You can even say hello to him. He won't bite you." Grandma said.

Jenny looked at the spider. It was still on the wall, but it didn't seem so scary anymore. It looked like a fuzzy ball with legs. Jenny felt a little braver.

"Hello, spider." Jenny said softly.

The spider moved a little, as if it heard her. Jenny smiled.

"See, Jenny? He's friendly. He likes you." Grandma said.

Jenny nodded. She felt better. She hugged grandma and thanked her.

"Thank you, grandma. You're the best. You always comfort me when I'm scared." Jenny said.

"You're welcome, Jenny. I love you very much. You always make me happy." Grandma said.

They hugged and kissed. Then they went back to the couch and finished the book. Jenny learned that spiders are not so bad, and grandma learned that Jenny is very smart. They had a wonderful day together.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Lily had a round ball that she liked to bounce and catch. Ben had a funny hat that he liked to wear and make faces.

"Look at me, Lily!" Ben said, putting the hat on his head. "I am a silly monkey!"

Lily laughed and threw the ball to him. "Catch, monkey!"

Ben tried to catch the ball, but he missed. The ball rolled under the sofa. "Oh no, where did it go?" Ben said, looking around.

Lily crawled to the sofa and lifted the edge. She saw the ball hiding in the dark. "I found it!" she said, reaching for it.

But as she touched the ball, it disappeared. Lily gasped and pulled her hand back. "What happened?" she said, scared.

Ben crawled to her and looked under the sofa. He saw nothing but dust. "The ball is gone!" he said, surprised.

They both stared at the empty space, wondering where the ball went. Then they heard a giggle from behind them. They turned around and saw their big sister, Mia, holding the ball. She had a remote control in her other hand.

"Gotcha!" Mia said, smiling. "This is not a real ball, it's a magic ball. I can make it disappear and appear with this button. Watch!"

She pressed the button and the ball vanished. She pressed it again and the ball came back. She did it a few more times, making the ball go on and off.

Lily and Ben were amazed and confused. They didn't know how Mia did that. They wanted to try the magic ball too.

"Can we play with it, Mia?" Lily asked, politely.

"Please, please, please?" Ben added, eagerly.

Mia thought for a moment. She liked to tease her little siblings, but she also liked to share. She decided to let them play with the ball, but only if they followed her rules.

"Okay, you can play with it, but only if you do what I say. And don't tell Mom or Dad, it's our secret. Deal?" Mia said, handing them the ball and the remote.

Lily and Ben nodded, excited. They agreed to do what Mia said. They didn't care about the rules, they just wanted to have fun with the magic ball. They thanked Mia and started to play with it, making it disappear and appear in different places. They laughed and giggled, enjoying the new game.

Mia watched them, smiling. She was happy to see them happy. She decided to join them and play with them. She put on the funny hat and pretended to be a silly monkey too. They all had a lot of fun with the magic ball and the funny hat. They didn't notice how fast the time passed, until they heard Mom calling them for dinner. They quickly hid the ball and the remote under the sofa and ran to the kitchen. They hoped Mom and Dad wouldn't find out about their secret. They wanted to play with the magic ball again tomorrow.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big, flexible snake. They could bend it and twist it and make it look like different things. Sometimes they pretended it was a rope, or a belt, or a scarf.

One night, they decided to sleep with the snake. They put it under their pillow and cuddled with it. They felt warm and cozy. They said good night to each other and closed their eyes.

But in the middle of the night, Lily woke up. She felt something cold and wet on her face. She opened her eyes and saw the snake. It was not a toy. It was a real snake. It had slithered out of the pillow and was licking her cheek. She screamed and jumped out of the bed.

Ben woke up too. He saw the snake and shivered. He was scared. He grabbed his pillow and threw it at the snake. The snake hissed and moved away. It crawled out of the window and disappeared.

Lily and Ben ran to their mom and dad. They told them what happened. Mom and dad hugged them and calmed them down. They checked their room and found no more snakes. They gave them new pillows and tucked them in. They said they were brave and they loved them.

Lily and Ben learned a lesson. They never played with the snake again. They only played with their other toys, like their dolls and cars and blocks. They were happy and safe.

Jill and Ben were sleeping in their beds. They had a big day tomorrow. They were going to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They were very excited to see the animals and the colors.

But in the middle of the night, they heard a loud noise. It sounded like a roar. They woke up and saw a big shadow on the wall. It looked like a lion. They were very scared.

"Ben, what is that?" Jill whispered.

"I don't know, Jill. Maybe it's a bad dream," Ben said.

They hid under their blankets and hoped the noise would go away. But it didn't. It got louder and closer. They felt something move their beds. They felt something breathe on their faces. They felt something bite their toes.

They screamed and cried. But Mom and Dad didn't come. They were too late. The lion had broken into their house and found them. The lion was hungry and angry. The lion ate them up.

The end.

Lily saw what Max did and was very sad and angry. She cried and shouted at Max. "Give me back my notebook! You ruined it! You are a bad brother!"

Max saw Lily's tears and heard her voice. He felt sorry for what he did. He did not mean to hurt Lily. He wanted to make her happy. He said to Lily, "I am sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I wanted to draw with you, but I did not ask. I did not know you liked your notebook so much. Can I help you fix it?"

Lily looked at Max and saw his sorry face. She was still sad, but she was not angry anymore. She said to Max, "Thank you, Max. I am glad you are sorry. You can help me fix it. We can use stickers and glue and new paper. We can make it better. We can draw together, but you have to ask me first. OK?"

Max nodded and smiled. He said, "OK, Lily. I will ask you first. I love you, Lily. You are a good sister."

Lily hugged Max and said, "I love you too, Max. You are a good brother."

They took the notebook and went to find stickers and glue and new paper. They worked together to fix the notebook. They made it more colorful and beautiful. They increased their drawings and their love. They were happy with their notebook.

Tom liked to sign. He learned how to sign from his mom, who was deaf. He could sign hello, thank you, and many other words. He wanted to show his friends at school how to sign, too.

One day, he brought a book of signs to his classroom. He asked his teacher if he could share it with the class. His teacher said yes, and gave him some time to talk. Tom was happy. He opened the book and started to sign.

He signed the word for cat, and pointed to a picture of a cat. He signed the word for dog, and pointed to a picture of a dog. He signed the word for bird, and pointed to a picture of a bird. He signed the word for fish, and pointed to a picture of a fish. He signed the word for turtle, and pointed to a picture of a turtle.

But then, he saw a picture of a snake. He did not like snakes. He was afraid of snakes. He did not want to sign the word for snake. He closed the book and said, "No more signs."

His teacher asked him why he stopped. Tom said, "I don't like snakes. They are scary. They can bite you and make you dead."

His teacher smiled and said, "Don't worry, Tom. The snake in the book is not real. It can't hurt you. And not all snakes are bad. Some snakes are friendly and helpful. Do you want to learn the sign for snake?"

Tom shook his head. He did not want to learn the sign for snake. He said, "Maybe another day. Today, I want to sign something else."

He opened the book again and looked for a picture of something he liked. He found a picture of a cake. He smiled and signed the word for cake. He said, "I like cake. Cake is yummy. Do you like cake?"

His teacher nodded and said, "I like cake, too. And I like your signs. You are very good at signing, Tom. Thank you for sharing with us."

The class clapped and cheered for Tom. Tom felt proud and happy. He liked to sign. He liked to share. He liked his teacher and his friends. He liked his classroom. He liked everything. Except snakes.

But then a big dog came running to them. The dog was fierce and barked loud. He wanted the yellow ball. He jumped and snatched the ball from Ben's hands. He ran away with the ball in his mouth.

Lily was brave. She ran after the dog. She waved her arms and yelled, "Stop! Drop the ball!"

The dog stopped and looked at Lily. He saw that she was not afraid. He dropped the ball and wagged his tail. He wanted to play.

Ben came out from behind Lily. He smiled and caught the ball. He threw it to the dog. The dog chased the ball and brought it back. He licked Ben's face.

Ben and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. They had a big pot, some water, and many spoons.

"Let's make soup!" said Ben. He poured some water into the pot and put it on the stove. He turned the knob to make the fire.

"Okay!" said Lily. She looked for something to put in the soup. She saw a jar of jam on the counter. She opened it and took a wide spoon. She scooped some jam and put it in the pot.

"Yuck!" said Ben. "Jam is not for soup! Jam is for bread!"

Lily did not understand. She liked jam. She thought it would make the soup sweet and red. She wanted to tell Ben, but she did not know how to say it. She remembered that Mommy taught her some signs with her hands. She made a sign for jam by rubbing her fingers together. She pointed to the pot and smiled.

Ben saw her sign. He knew what it meant. He shook his head. He made a sign for soup by pretending to sip from a bowl. He pointed to the pot and frowned.

Lily saw his sign. She knew what it meant. She felt sad. She did not want to make Ben unhappy. She wanted to make him happy. She thought of something else to put in the soup. She saw a can of beans on the shelf. She opened it and took another spoon. She dumped some beans in the pot.

"Good!" said Ben. "Beans are good for soup! Beans are yummy and healthy!"

Lily felt happy. She made Ben happy. She made a sign for good by giving a thumbs up. She pointed to the pot and nodded.

Ben saw her sign. He smiled. He made a sign for good too. He hugged Lily and said, "You are a good chef! And a good sister!"

They both laughed and waited for the soup to be ready. They hoped Mommy and Daddy would like it too.

Tom and Mia liked to ride their bikes in the park. They had red bikes with bells and baskets. They always wore helmets and gloves to be safe. One day, they saw a new path in the park. It was narrow and twisty and had a sign that said "Dangerous. Do not enter."

"Let's go there!" Tom said. He was brave and curious. He wanted to see what was on the other side of the path.

"No, Tom, we can't!" Mia said. She was careful and smart. She knew the sign meant the path was not for bikes. "It's too dangerous. We might fall or get hurt."

But Tom did not listen to Mia. He rode his bike past the sign and into the path. Mia followed him, because she did not want him to go alone. She was scared and worried.

The path was bumpy and steep. There were rocks and roots and holes. Tom and Mia had to pedal hard and steer well. They saw many things on the path. They saw birds and bugs and flowers. They saw a big tree with a hole. They saw a pile of herbs that smelled good.

"Look, Mia, herbs!" Tom said. He stopped his bike and got off. He picked some herbs and put them in his basket. He liked herbs. He liked to smell them and taste them.

"Tom, we have to go back!" Mia said. She did not like herbs. She did not like the path. She wanted to go back to the park. She saw something in the hole of the tree. It was big and furry and had sharp teeth. It was a bear. "Tom, there's a bear!"

Tom looked up and saw the bear. He was scared and sorry. He wished he had listened to Mia. He wished he had not entered the path. He got on his bike and rang his bell. He hoped the bear would not chase them.

"Come on, Mia, let's ride fast!" Tom said. He and Mia rode their bikes as fast as they could. They dodged the rocks and roots and holes. They did not look back. They reached the end of the path and the park. They were safe and happy.

They hugged each other and their bikes. They learned a lesson. They decided to never go on the dangerous path again. They decided to always follow the signs and listen to each other. They rode their bikes back home and told their mom and dad what happened. They gave them some herbs and said sorry. They said they loved them and thanked them for their bikes. They said they would be good and careful from now on.

Sometimes, things like that happen when we play. It doesn't mean you have to be mad at each other. You can still be friends and share your horses."

Anna liked to observe the birds in the garden. She saw how they flew in the sky, how they sang on the trees, how they ate the seeds she gave them. She wanted to be friends with them, but they were shy and flew away when she came near.

One day, she had an idea. She took a long string from her room and tied one end to a stick. She put some seeds on the other end of the string and laid it on the grass. Then she hid behind a bush and waited.

Soon, a little bird came and saw the seeds. It hopped closer and closer, until it reached the string. It pecked at the seeds and ate them. Anna was very happy. She pulled the string gently, hoping to bring the bird closer to her.

But the bird felt the string move and got scared. It flapped its wings and tried to fly away. But the string was stuck on its leg. It cried out and struggled, but it could not get free.

Anna felt sorry for the bird. She did not want to hurt it. She ran out of her hiding place and went to the bird. She said, "Don't be afraid, little bird. I just wanted to play with you. I will let you go. You are so graceful and pretty. I like you very much."

She untied the string from the bird's leg and held it in her hand. The bird was still scared, but it calmed down a little. It looked at Anna with its bright eyes and chirped softly. Anna smiled and stroked its feathers. Then she opened her hand and let the bird fly away.

The bird soared in the sky and sang a happy song. Anna waved at it and said, "Goodbye, little bird. Thank you for being my friend. Come back soon." She watched the bird until it disappeared. Then she went back to her room and put the string away. She hoped to see the bird again. She felt happy and proud. She had observed a bird up close.

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to help their mom in the kitchen. One day, mom asked them to sort the vegetables for dinner. She gave them a big bowl of cauliflower, carrots, peas, and corn.

"Sort them by color, please," mom said. "Put the white ones here, the orange ones there, the green ones here, and the yellow ones there."

Lila and Ben nodded and started to sort the vegetables. Lila liked cauliflower, so she put a lot of it in the white pile. Ben liked corn, so he put a lot of it in the yellow pile. They did not like carrots or peas, so they put only a few of them in the orange and green piles.

Mom came back and saw the uneven piles. She frowned and said, "Lila and Ben, this is not fair. You have to share the vegetables equally. You can't take more of what you like and leave less of what you don't like. That is selfish and rude."

Lila and Ben felt ashamed and said, "Sorry, mom. We did not mean to be selfish and rude. We just like cauliflower and corn more than carrots and peas."

Mom smiled and said, "I understand, but you have to try new things sometimes. You might find out that you like them too. And you have to think of others who might like different things than you. How would you feel if someone took all the cauliflower or corn and left you none?"

Lila and Ben thought about it and said, "We would feel sad and angry."

Mom nodded and said, "Exactly. So, let's sort the vegetables again, and this time, make sure each pile has the same amount. Then, we can cook them and add some butter and salt and pepper. They will taste sweet and yummy, I promise."

Lila and Ben agreed and sorted the vegetables again. They made sure each pile had the same amount. Then, they helped mom cook them and put them on the table. They tried a bite of each vegetable and found out that they were all sweet and yummy, just like mom said. They thanked mom for the dinner and learned to share and try new things.

Sam likes to imagine that he is a builder. He has a fake hammer that he uses to hit things. He pretends that he is making a house or a car or a boat.

One day, he finds a real hammer in the garage. He thinks it is a bigger and better fake hammer. He wants to try it out. He takes it to his room and looks for something to hit.

He sees his teddy bear on the bed. He thinks it would be fun to hit the teddy bear with the hammer. He lifts the hammer and swings it down.

"Ow!" the teddy bear says. "That hurts!"

Sam is surprised. He drops the hammer and looks at the teddy bear. The teddy bear has a hole in its head and some stuffing is coming out.

"I'm sorry, teddy bear," Sam says. "I didn't know you could talk. I didn't know this was a real hammer. I thought it was a fake hammer."

The teddy bear sighs. "It's okay, Sam. I know you didn't mean to hurt me. But please don't use the real hammer again. Use the fake hammer. It's safer and more fun."

Sam nods. He hugs the teddy bear and says he is sorry again. He puts the real hammer back in the garage and takes the fake hammer to his room. He imagines that he is a builder again, but this time he only hits things that don't talk.

"Can we feed the elephant, mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey. Here, take some carrots from this bag. But be careful and gentle, okay?" mom said.

Lily and Sam took some carrots and walked to the fence where the elephant was. They held out their hands and the elephant came closer. It used its nose to take the carrots and eat them. Lily and Sam giggled.

But Sam wanted more fun. He saw a ball on the ground. He picked it up and threw it at the elephant. The ball hit the elephant's ear and bounced back. The elephant did not like that. It made a loud noise and shook its head.

"Sam, don't do that! That's not nice!" Lily said.

But Sam did not listen. He threw the ball again. And again. And again. The elephant got angry. It kicked the fence with its foot. The fence broke. The elephant ran out. It chased Sam.

"Sam, run!" Lily shouted.

But Sam was too slow. The elephant caught him. It lifted him with its nose and threw him in the air. Sam screamed. He fell on the ground. He was hurt.

Mom ran to Sam. She hugged him and cried. She called for help. Lily was scared and sad. She wished Sam had not thrown the ball. She wished the elephant had not kicked the fence. She wished they had not come to the zoo.

But they did not see the car coming. The car drove fast and hit the puddle. The water sprayed all over Ben and Lily. They got wet and dirty. They also got scared. The car honked and the driver shouted.

"Hey, you kids! Get out of the road! You are making a mess!"

Ben and Lily ran out of the puddle. They put on their shoes and socks. They felt ashamed. They knew they did something wrong. They said sorry to the driver. They said sorry to their mom. They said sorry to each other.

They learned a lesson. They should not play in the puddle near the road. They should wait for the flood to go away. They should be careful and safe. They hoped the park would be dry soon. They wanted to play at the park again.

Anna is not impressed. She says, "Your car is stupid, Tom. It is too big and loud. It does not fit on the floor. It will hit the wall and break. My car is smaller and quieter. It can turn and stop. It is smarter than yours."

Tom is sad and angry. He says, "Oh no, my car is broken. It was my favorite car. It was not stupid, it was awesome. Why did it have to break?" He starts to cry.

Anna feels sorry for Tom. She says, "I'm sorry, Tom. Your car was not stupid, it was just too fast. Maybe you can fix it or get a new one. Do you want to play with my car? We can share it and have fun."

Tom stops crying and looks at Anna. He says, "Thank you, Anna. You are a good friend. Your car is not smarter, it is just different. We can play with it and have fun. Maybe we can get a new car together. One that can increase its speed and turn and stop. That would be the best car ever."

Tom and Lily were twins who lived on a farm with their mom and dad. They liked to play with the animals and help with the chores. One day, their dad told them he had to go to the market and sell some wheat. Wheat was a plant that they grew in the fields and made bread and cakes with.

"Can we go with you, dad?" Tom asked.

"Please, dad, please!" Lily begged.

Their dad smiled and said, "Okay, but you have to be good and stay close to me. The market is very busy and there are many people there."

Tom and Lily were happy and jumped into the wagon with their dad. They saw many things on the way, like horses, cows, sheep, and pigs. They also saw a big house with a fence and a gate. It belonged to a wealthy man who had a lot of money and land.

"Wow, look at that house!" Tom said. "It's so big and pretty!"

"I wish we could live there," Lily said. "They must have a lot of toys and candy."

Their dad shook his head and said, "Don't be silly, children. That house is not as nice as it looks. The wealthy man is very mean and greedy. He doesn't share with anyone and he treats his workers badly. He also wants to buy our farm and make us leave. We don't want to be like him. We have enough wheat and love to be happy."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "You're right, dad. We love our farm and our family."

They soon arrived at the market and their dad parked the wagon near a stall. He told Tom and Lily to stay in the wagon and watch the wheat while he went to talk to a buyer. He said he would be back soon and gave them each a kiss.

Tom and Lily waited in the wagon and looked around. They saw many people selling and buying different things, like fruits, vegetables, eggs, cheese, and meat. They also saw some toys, like dolls, balls, and cars. They wished they could have some of them, but they knew they were too expensive.

Then they saw a man walking towards them. He was wearing a fancy suit and a hat. He had a big nose and a thin mouth. He looked like the wealthy man who owned the big house.

"Hello, children," he said in a sneaky voice. "What do you have here?"

Tom and Lily felt scared and said, "This is our dad's wheat. He's selling it at the market. Please go away."

The man laughed and said, "Your dad's wheat? I don't think so. This is my wheat now. I'm going to take it and sell it for a lot of money. And you know what? I'm also going to buy your farm and make you leave. You have no choice. You're poor and I'm rich."

He grabbed a sack of wheat and threw it into his cart. He did the same with the other sacks. Tom and Lily cried and shouted, "Stop! Stop! That's not fair! That's not yours! Please give it back!"

But the man didn't listen. He whipped his horse and drove away with the wheat. He laughed and said, "Too bad, children. You lose. I win. Goodbye!"

Tom and Lily were left alone in the empty wagon. They hugged each other and sobbed. They didn't know what to do. They wondered where their dad was and if he would come back. They felt very sad and afraid.

The end.

When they got home, they ran to the kitchen and opened their candy. Lily bit into her heart candy and made a face. It was sour and sharp. It hurt her tongue and made her eyes water. She spit it out and cried. "Mom, this candy is bad. It is sharp and ouchy. I don't like it," she said.

Max bit into his star candy and made a face. It was hard and crunchy. It broke his tooth and made him bleed. He spit it out and cried. "Mom, this candy is bad. It is hard and ouchy. I don't like it," he said.

Mom heard their cries and came to the kitchen. She saw their candy and their faces. She felt sorry for them and hugged them. "I'm sorry, my loves. Those candy are not good for you. They are sharp and hard and ouchy. They are not real candy. They are fake candy. They are bad for your teeth and your tongue. You should not eat them," she said.

She threw away the candy and gave them each a glass of water. She also gave them each a real candy. A soft and sweet and chewy candy. A candy that made them happy and cheerful. A candy that they liked. They thanked mom and ate their candy. They smiled and hugged mom. They learned their lesson. They never picked fake candy again. They only picked real candy. The end.

Lily saw what happened. She was scared. She did not want to slide down. She wanted to help Ben. But she did not know how to get down. She was stuck on the slide.

"Help, help!" Lily shouted. She hoped someone would hear her. But the park was quiet. There was no one else there. Lily felt alone and sad.

"Lily, Ben, what happened?" she asked. She was worried.

"Mom, Ben slipped on a staff and fell. He's hurt. And I can't get down. I'm scared," Lily said.

"Don't worry, sweetie. I'm here. I'll help you," mom said. She climbed up the ladder and reached Lily. She hugged her and lifted her down. Then, she went to Ben and checked his knee. It was not too bad. Just a scratch. She cleaned it and put a band-aid on it.

"There, there. You'll be fine. It was an accident. Next time, be careful and look where you slide," mom said.

"Thank you, mom. You're the best," Ben said.

"Thank you, mom. I love you," Lily said.

Mom smiled and hugged them both. She was glad they were okay. She took them home and gave them some cookies and milk. They felt better and learned a lesson. They never slid on a wet slide again.

One day, a little cat was playing in the park. He saw a big human sitting on a bench. The human had a shiny thing in his hand. The cat was curious. He wanted to see the shiny thing.

The cat sneaked behind the bench. He waited for the right moment. Then he jumped on the bench and pushed the shiny thing with his paw. The shiny thing fell on the ground and broke into pieces. The human was angry. He shouted at the cat.

"Bad cat! You broke my phone! Go away!" The human said.

The cat was scared. He ran away from the human. He hid under a slide. He felt sorry for what he did. He wished he had not pushed the shiny thing.

Another cat came to the slide. He saw the little cat. He asked him what was wrong.

"I pushed a shiny thing and broke it. The human was mad at me. I did a bad thing." The little cat said.

The other cat nodded. He said, "I know how you feel. I once pushed a flower pot and made a mess. The human was mad at me too. But I learned my lesson. You should not push things that are not yours. You should be careful and respectful."

The little cat understood. He said, "You are right. I should not push things that are not mine. I should be careful and respectful. I want to say sorry to the human. But I am afraid he will be mad at me again."

The other cat said, "Don't be afraid. The human might be mad, but he might also forgive you. You should be brave and honest. Maybe he will give you another chance."

The little cat agreed. He said, "Thank you for helping me. You are a good friend. I will be brave and honest. I will say sorry to the human."

The little cat and the other cat went to the bench. The human was still there. He looked sad. The little cat approached him. He meowed softly. He looked at the human with his big eyes. He tried to say sorry.

The human saw the little cat. He was surprised. He saw the other cat too. He realized they were friends. He felt a little less angry. He said, "What do you want, cat? Do you want to break something else?"

The little cat shook his head. He nudged the broken shiny thing with his nose. He meowed again. He tried to say sorry.

The human understood. He saw the little cat was sorry. He felt a little less sad. He said, "You broke my phone, cat. It was very important to me. It had pictures and messages and music. But I see you are sorry. You are brave and honest. I forgive you, cat. But don't do it again."

The little cat was happy. He purred. He licked the human's hand. He thanked him.

The human smiled. He petted the little cat. He thanked him too.

The other cat was proud. He said, "You did well, little cat. You learned your lesson. You should not push things that are not yours. You should be careful and respectful. You should be brave and honest. You are a good cat."

The little cat nodded. He said, "You are right. I learned my lesson. I should not push things that are not mine. I should be careful and respectful. I should be brave and honest. I am a good cat. And you are a good friend."

The little cat and the other cat played in the park. The human watched them. He was happy. He learned his lesson too. He should not be too mad at cats. He should be kind and forgiving. He should be happy and grateful. He was a good human. And they were good friends.

"What are you doing?" she asked.

"Why?" Mom asked.

"Because it's interesting!" Sara and Ben said.

Mom shook her head. She explained to them that the freezer was not a toy, but a place to keep food cold. She told them that they could not open it without the key, and that the key was only for grown-ups. She said that they could hurt themselves or spoil the food if they tried to open it.

She also told them that crying and kicking was not a good way to solve problems. She said that they should ask for help or find something else to do if they could not get what they wanted.

She hugged them and dried their tears. She asked them to say sorry to the freezer and to each other. She also gave them a cookie and a glass of milk.

Sara and Ben said sorry to the freezer and to each other. They ate their cookie and drank their milk. They felt better.

They learned that the freezer was not interesting, but important. They also learned that crying and kicking was not helpful, but asking and listening was. They decided to play with their toys instead. They had fun.

Timmy thought for a moment and said, "Sure, you can pass by and get some nuts. But please don't take my sandwich." The squirrel agreed and went on his way. Timmy continued to fish and caught a big fish. He was so happy that he forgot all about his sandwich. He went home with a big smile on his face, proud of his catch. The end.

Steve was thrilled and immediately gulped down the hot stew. But after finishing the meal, he realized something strange was happening. He felt like he was shrinking! Although he was scared, Steve managed to stay brave and faced his neighbor.

"See, it wasn't so bad after all," Mummy said. "Now let's continue our walk and enjoy the beauty of the forest."

Tommy smiled and he and his mother walked through the forest together, admiring the pale and symmetrical patterns of the trees.

Abbie smiled, and said out loud: "Wow! I can keep it!"

All of a sudden, Abbie felt like someone was watching her. She turned around and saw a big snowy wolf right behind her. Abbie screamed and started to run away, but the wolf was quick and it followed her.

Abbie was so scared, but she kept running away. Suddenly, she slipped on the icy steel path and fell down.

The wolf stopped and it looked at Abbie. She was too scared to move.

The wolf just nodded at her, and it turned around and went away.

Abbie was so relieved! She stood up and walked carefully back home. She put the steel coin on her shelf, like a reminder of her brave adventure.

The End.

The moral of the story is that we should put things away after we use them, or else they will soon become empty.

Timmy said, "Oh no! That's not good. Can I help?" The soldier said, "Yes, you can help me open the water hose." Timmy opened the water hose and the soldier put out the fire. Timmy felt happy that he could help the soldier.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to talk. She talked all day long, even when she was eating or playing with her toys. One day, Lily's mom took her to the library. As soon as they walked inside, Lily noticed how quiet it was. "Why is it so quiet?" she asked her mom. "Well, people come here to read and they need silence so they can concentrate," her mom explained.

Lily thought it was weird that everyone was so quiet. She wanted to talk to the other kids there, but her mom reminded her about the silence rule. "Oh, I see," Lily said. She tried to be quiet but it was hard for her. Finally, she found a book that she liked and started to read. She was so into the story that she didn't even notice the silence anymore.

After a while, Lily's mom said it was time to go. Lily asked if they could come back to the library again. "Of course we can," her mom said. "It's a great place to read and learn new things." Lily smiled and said, "I like learning new things. Thanks for explaining it to me, Mom."

One day, Benny saw something shiny on the ground. He flew down and picked it up. It was a long arrow. Benny had an idea. He told Remy, "I will hide this arrow, and you must hurry to find it!" Remy agreed, excited for the new game.

Benny hid the arrow behind a big tree and told Remy to start looking. Remy hurried all around the forest, searching high and low. Finally, he found the arrow behind the big tree. Remy was so happy! He and Benny played the arrow game all day long, and they had the best time ever.

A tiny child named Tom walked around the colorful store aisle with eyes wide. Tom was searching for the perfect crib for his new baby brother. 

An old lady, Mrs. Brown, stopped near Tom and smiled.
"What you looking for, sweetheart?" She asked.
Tom excitedly shared that he wanted to buy a crib.

Mrs. Brown shook her head.
"No," she said, her voice harsh. "Your brother doesn't need a crib. He'll outgrow it too quickly."

Tom frowned. He didn't want his brother to miss out on anything.

Mrs. Brown placed a gentle hand on Tom's shoulder. "Your brother needs something better and more permanent. He needs a bed. A big comfy bed so he can sleep through the night."

After a little more shopping, Tom proudly bought a bed for his brother with the support of Mrs. Brown.

The moral of the story is that it's important to think ahead when making decisions, and to not always go with the first thought. If Tom had not listened to Mrs. Brown, his brother would have been stuck with a too-small crib.

Her mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it's very pretty. But be careful, it might be sharp." 

Lily nodded and held the chain carefully. She wanted to wear it as a necklace, but it was too big for her. 

"It's too big, mommy. Can you make it easy for me to wear?" asked Lily. 

Her mommy took the chain and made it shorter so that it fit perfectly around Lily's neck. Lily was very happy and wore it all day long.

After a few days, the bird's wing was all better. Sam held the bird and said, "Now you can fly again, little bird." The bird chirped and flew up into the sky. Sam waved goodbye to the bird and went back to his busy life as a sailor. He always remembered the little bird he had helped, and it made him smile.

Timmy's mom said, "Remember to take care of your things or you might lose them forever." Timmy learned his lesson and promised to be more careful with his toys from now on. Even though Timmy never found his toy car again, he knew to always take care of his things and not lose his memories.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety was very happy because he had learned to whistle. He would whistle all day long and all the other birds would come to listen to him.

One day, Tweety decided to show off his whistling skills to his friends. He flew to a nearby tree where his friends were sitting and started to whistle. But, to his surprise, none of his friends were impressed. They said Tweety's whistle was too loud and it hurt their ears.

Tweety was sad and his feathers turned pale. He didn't understand why his friends didn't like his whistle. He flew away to a quiet place and sat on a scale to think. Suddenly, he heard a voice, "Don't be sad, Tweety. Your whistle is beautiful, but it's just too loud for us. If you whistle softly, we will love it."

Tweety looked around and saw a wise old owl sitting on a branch. He listened to the owl's advice and started to whistle softly. His friends heard it and came to listen. They loved it and Tweety was happy again. From that day on, Tweety would whistle softly and all his friends would come to listen to him.

"Are you okay, Lily?" her mom asked.

Lily nodded and said, "I slipped, but I'm okay. Can we go see the fish in the river now?"

As she was drinking, she noticed a little lizard sitting nearby. The lizard was very patient and didn't move at all. Tweety thought it was funny how the lizard didn't blink his eyes like she did. Blink means to close your eyes quickly and then open them again.

His mom thought it was neat too, and they put the leaf in a jar so they could watch the caterpillar grow into a butterfly. 

Every day, Timmy would check on the caterpillar and see how much it had grown. He loved watching it change and transform. Finally, one day, the caterpillar turned into a beautiful green butterfly. Timmy was so excited that he ran outside to show his friends. They all thought it was amazing and they played together in the backyard all day. The end.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to make mud pies and pretend they were chefs. They used old pots and spoons and added grass and flowers to their pies.

"Look, this is my jelly pie!" Lily said, showing Tom her round mud pie. "It is very delicate. You have to be careful."

Tom nodded and smiled. He wanted to try Lily's jelly pie. He reached out his hand and touched the mud. It was wet and sticky. He pulled his hand back and made a face.

"Yuck, this is not jelly!" he said. "This is mud. Jelly is sweet and soft. Mud is dirty and hard."

Lily frowned. She did not like Tom's words. She thought her jelly pie was nice. She had worked hard to make it.

"No, this is jelly!" she said. "You just have to wait. It will dry in the sun and then it will be jelly. You are silly, Tom. You don't know anything."

Tom shook his head. He did not believe Lily. He thought she was wrong. He did not want to wait. He wanted real jelly, not mud.

"Fine, you can have your mud pie. I don't want it. I will go and ask Mom for real jelly. She has some in the fridge. Come on, let's go." he said.

He got up and ran to the house. Lily stayed in the garden. She looked at her jelly pie. She hoped it would dry soon and become jelly. She wanted to prove Tom wrong. She wanted to show him her jelly pie was the best.

Tom is a squirrel who likes to play all day. He does not like to clean his nest or find nuts for winter. He thinks it is too hard and boring. He likes to run, jump and chase his friends in the park.

One day, he sees a big, light nut on a branch. He wants to eat it. He runs to the branch and tries to grab the nut. But the nut is not a nut. It is a trap. A net falls on Tom and he is stuck. He is scared and sad.

Lily is another squirrel who likes to work. She cleans her nest every day and finds many nuts for winter. She thinks it is fun and good. She likes to help her friends and family in the park.

She sees Tom in the net and hears him cry. She runs to him and tries to help. She bites the net and makes a hole. She tells Tom to crawl out. Tom is free and happy. He thanks Lily and hugs her.

Tom learns a lesson. He learns that playing is good, but working is also good. He learns that cleaning and finding nuts are important for squirrels. He learns that being lazy and greedy can be bad. He decides to help Lily and other squirrels with their work. He becomes a good and smart squirrel.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the attic. The attic was a big room under the roof, where they kept old things and toys. They could find many fun things to do there, like dress up, read books, or make forts.

One day, they found a big box in the corner of the attic. It was covered with dust and had a long rope tied around it. Ben and Lily were curious and wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's open it!" Ben said.

"OK, but be careful. Maybe it has something scary or breakable in it." Lily said.

They pulled the rope and opened the box. Inside, they saw a lot of shiny balls of different colors and sizes. They looked like Christmas decorations, but they were not.

"What are these?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. They are pretty. Can we touch them?" Lily asked.

They reached for the balls, but as soon as they touched them, something strange happened. The balls started to grow bigger and bigger. They filled the box and spilled out of it. They rolled around the attic and bumped into the walls and the furniture. They increased so much that they almost pushed Ben and Lily out of the door.

"Help! What is happening?" Ben shouted.

"I don't know! How do we stop them?" Lily cried.

They ran out of the attic and down the stairs. They looked for their mom and dad, who were in the kitchen.

"Mom! Dad! Come quick! There are big balls in the attic!" Ben and Lily said.

"What? Big balls? What are you talking about?" Mom and Dad said.

They followed Ben and Lily to the attic. They saw the balls that had grown so big that they filled the whole room. They were amazed and confused.

"Where did these come from? How did they get so big?" Mom asked.

"We found them in a box. We touched them and they increased. We don't know why." Lily said.

One day, Lily and her mom went to the store to buy some cheese. Lily saw a big wheel of cheese on a shelf. It looked so yummy and round. She wanted to taste it. She asked her mom, "Can I have some cheese, please?"

Her mom said, "Not now, Lily. We have to pay for it first. And this cheese is not for us. It is for someone else who ordered it. We have to find the cheese that is available for us."

Lily did not understand. She thought all cheese was for everyone. She did not want to wait. She wanted to have some cheese now. She reached for the big wheel of cheese and pulled it off the shelf.

But the cheese was too heavy for Lily. It slipped from her hands and rolled away. It bumped into a cart, a basket, a can, and a jar. It made a lot of noise. Everyone in the store looked at Lily and the cheese.

Lily was scared. She did not mean to make a mess. She did not want to get in trouble. She started to cry. She yelled, "I'm sorry! I'm sorry! I just wanted some cheese!"

Her mom ran to her and hugged her. She said, "It's okay, Lily. It was an accident. You didn't know. But next time, you have to listen to me and be careful. Cheese is good, but not all cheese is for us. We have to share and be polite."

Lily nodded. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you. And I love cheese. But not this cheese. Can we find some cheese that is for us?"

Her mom smiled. She said, "Yes, we can. Come on, let's go and find some cheese that is available for us. And maybe some cookies, too."

Lily smiled, too. She said, "Okay, mom. Let's go. And thank you for the cheese. And the cookies."

They walked away, holding hands. The store manager came and picked up the big wheel of cheese. He was not happy. He said, "Who did this? Who messed up my cheese?"

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big yellow banana on a bench. Sara and Tom both want the banana.

"Can I have the banana?" Sara asks.

"No, I saw it first!" Tom says.

They start to fight over the banana. They pull and tug and shout. They are not polite to each other.

A man sees them fighting. He is angry. He walks to the bench. He grabs the banana.

"Hey, this is my banana!" he says. "You two are very rude. You should learn to share and say sorry."

He peels the banana and eats it. He throws the peel on the ground.

Sara and Tom are sad. They lost the banana. They look at the peel. They feel sorry.

They rush to the man. They want to say sorry. But it is too late. The man is gone.

They step on the peel. They slip and fall. They hurt themselves. They cry.

The end.

"Look, Lily, this is a sweet carrot. It is like candy, but better. Do you want to try it?" Mommy asked.

Lily was curious. She liked honey. She liked sweet things. She looked at the carrot. It was orange and shiny. She reached out and took it from Mommy. She put it in her mouth and bit it.

It was sweet and crunchy and juicy. It was yummy. Lily smiled. She liked the sweet carrot. She wanted more.

"Can I have another one, Mommy?" Lily asked.

Mommy smiled too. She was happy. She gave Lily another sweet carrot. And another. And another. Lily ate them all. She even tried some lettuce and cheese. She liked them too.

"See, Lily, vegetables are yummy. You just have to try them. You are a good girl," Mommy said.

Lily nodded. She felt good. She ate her salad. She was strong and healthy and smart. She liked vegetables. Well, some of them.

Anna and Ben were playing in the old house. They liked to pretend they were explorers and find new things. But today, they heard a strange noise from the attic. It sounded like a moan.

"Did you hear that?" Anna asked Ben.

"Yes, I did. Maybe it's a ghost!" Ben said.

They were both scared, but curious. They decided to go up the stairs and see what it was. They held hands and walked slowly.

When they reached the attic, they saw a big box. The noise was coming from inside. They opened the lid and saw a cat. The cat was old and sick. It looked at them with sad eyes.

"Hello, kitty. Are you the ghost?" Anna said.

The cat meowed softly. It was not a ghost. It was just a lonely animal.

"Maybe he needs help. Maybe he's hungry and thirsty," Ben said.

They felt sorry for the cat. They decided to discuss what to do. They talked quietly and agreed to take the cat home with them. They hoped their mom and dad would let them keep it.

They wrapped the cat in a blanket and carried it downstairs. They were happy they found a new friend. They learned that sometimes things are not what they seem. They also learned to be kind and brave.

Ben and Lily were restless. They wanted to play outside, but it was raining. They looked out the window and saw puddles and worms. They did not like puddles and worms.

"Can we hop, Mom?" Ben asked. He liked to hop on one foot and make funny noises.

"Not inside, Ben. You will make a mess and break things," Mom said. She was busy making lunch.

"Can we paint, Mom?" Lily asked. She liked to paint with bright colors and make shapes.

"Yes, you can paint, but be careful. Don't spill the paint or get it on your clothes," Mom said. She gave them some paper, brushes and paint.

Ben and Lily started to paint. They painted flowers, trees, birds and suns. They were happy for a while, but soon they got bored. They wanted to paint something else.

"I know! Let's paint eggs!" Ben said. He had an idea.

"Eggs? How do we paint eggs?" Lily asked. She was curious.

"Look, Mom has some eggs in the fridge. We can take them and paint them. Then we can hide them and find them. Like a game!" Ben said. He was excited.

"Okay, let's do it!" Lily said. She was eager.

They took some eggs from the fridge and brought them to the table. They painted them with different colors and patterns. They made them look pretty and funny. They were proud of their eggs.

"Now let's hide them!" Ben said. He took some eggs and ran to the living room. He hid them under the sofa, behind the curtains, on the bookshelf and in the vase.

"I'll hide mine too!" Lily said. She took some eggs and ran to the bedroom. She hid them under the bed, in the closet, on the dresser and in the toy box.

They finished hiding their eggs and went back to the table. They smiled at each other.

"Ready, set, go!" Ben said. He and Lily ran to find the eggs. They hopped from room to room, looking for the eggs. They laughed and shouted when they found them.

"Look, I found one!" Ben said. He held up a blue egg with yellow dots.

"Me too!" Lily said. She held up a pink egg with green stripes.

They found all the eggs and put them in a basket. They were happy and tired.

"Look, Mom, we painted eggs!" Ben said. He showed Mom the basket.

"They are very nice, Ben. But where did you get the eggs?" Mom asked. She looked at the basket and then at the fridge.

"From the fridge, Mom. We wanted to play a game," Ben said. He did not understand why Mom looked angry.

"Ben, Lily, you can't take the eggs from the fridge. They are for eating, not for painting. And you can't hide them in the house. They will go bad and smell. And you can't paint with the paint I gave you. It is not washable. It will stain the eggs and everything else. You made a big mess, Ben and Lily. You are in trouble," Mom said. She was very angry.

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They felt sorry and scared. They did not mean to make Mom angry. They did not know the eggs were for eating. They did not know the paint was not washable. They just wanted to have fun.

"Sorry, Mom. We didn't know. We were restless. We wanted to hop," Ben said.

"Sorry, Mom. We didn't know. We were restless. We wanted to paint," Lily said.

Mom sighed. She was still angry, but she also loved Ben and Lily. She knew they were restless. She knew they wanted to hop and paint. She knew they were just kids.

"It's okay, Ben and Lily. I forgive you. But you have to help me clean up the mess. And you have to promise me not to take the eggs from the fridge again. And you have to use washable paint next time. And you have to ask me before you play a game. Do you understand?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom. We understand. We promise. We love you, Mom," Ben and Lily said.

They hugged Mom and helped her clean up the mess. They learned their lesson. They were not restless anymore. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah who felt uncomfortable. She did not like the noisy bell that woke her up every morning. Whenever it rang, she would hold her ears and wish it would stop.

Every day Sarah put on her shoes and coat so she could walk to school. Before she walked out the door, the bell would ring and Sarah would hate it. She hated the sound and hated having to leave her comfortable house.

One day, Sarah decided she wasn't going to listen to the bell anymore. She put on her shoes and coat but didn't walk out the door. Instead, she ran and hid under her bed. The bell still rang but it was muffled and Sarah didn't feel uncomfortable anymore.

Sarah stayed under her bed until her mother came and found her. She told Sarah that she had to go to school, no matter how much she hated the bell. Reluctantly, Sarah packed her things and went to school.

But Sarah had a plan. When the bell rang, she covered her ears and scrunched up her face. She tried to make the bell's sound less uncomfortable, and with a lot of practice it eventually worked. Now Sarah can hear the bell ring and not be so uncomfortable.

Once upon a time, there was a furry little bear. She wanted to explore the world, but she was scared to go too far from home. 

One day, she decided to take a walk. She was walking along and suddenly it started to snow. She felt a chill in the air and shivered in her fur. 

Suddenly, she heard a loud crack! She stopped and noticed that the snow around her had frozen. She was frozen like a statue. 

She could barely move her legs, her arms, or her neck. She couldn't call for help. She was very scared.

Then she felt something warm. It was a friendly creature who was cuddling her fur and blowing warm breath on her neck! Slowly and carefully, he melted the snow around her until she was free to move again. 

She thanked her new friend, hugged him tight, and ran home to stay warm.

Once upon a time, there was a hot dinosaur. He was rather warm, but he was enjoying himself in the sun.

He saw a butterfly fluttering high in the sky, and he watched it flying for a while. Then, he had an idea. He called out to the butterfly, "Hey butterfly! Can you please help me? I have a request for you!"

The butterfly flew down and said, "What do you need my help with?" The dinosaur told the butterfly, "I'm very hot in this sun. Can you please fly up and make it a bit cooler down here?"

The butterfly said, "Of course I can try. I'll flap my wings and see if I can make it cooler." It flew up high and began to flap its wings rapidly. After a few minutes, the air around the dinosaur began to cool down.

The dinosaur was delighted! He thanked the butterfly and they both enjoyed the cooler air. The dinosaur and the butterfly were now fast friends, and they had many fun adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her puzzle. One day, she was so happy to finish her puzzle. She wanted to show it to her mom. But the puzzle was on a high shelf. She tried to reach it but she couldn't. 

Suddenly, her mom came into the room and saw her struggling. She picked her up and helped her touch the puzzle. Lily was so happy! She felt safe in her mom's arms. 

From that day on, Lily always asked for help when she needed it. She knew that her mom would keep her safe and help her touch anything she wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a soldier. He was a normal soldier who liked to march and wear his hat. One day, his phone rang. It was his mom calling to say she missed him. The soldier was happy to hear her voice and talked for a long time. When he hung up, he felt better and went back to his normal day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved trains very much. One day, she saw a big train passing by her house. She was so happy and excited, she ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, I saw a big train! Can we go see it again?"

Her mom said, "Sure, we can go see it again tomorrow."

The next day, Lily and her mom went to the train station. They saw the big train again. Lily said, "Mommy, the train is so fine! Can we ride on it?"

Her mom replied, "No, we can't ride on it today, but we can come back and see it again another day."

Lily was happy to see the train again and promised to repeat the visit soon.
